title: Terminal primitives, input and rendering
introduction: Worker fragment for packages/tui and native ice-tui primitives. Every finding is based on full source/test-body reads identified in tui-terminal-source-review.json; no tests or terminal processes were executed. Existing native capabilities are preserved and exact differences are enumerated.

entries.title: Consistent grapheme cell widths and output-only normalization
entries.what: Measure and navigate terminal cells consistently for Unicode, ANSI, tabs and streamed emoji, then normalize only the bytes written to the terminal.
entries.mechanism:
TS shares Intl.Segmenter instances for grapheme and word segmentation. Printable ASCII returns length directly; non-ASCII widths are cached in an insertion-order Map capped512, evicting its first key rather than refreshing access order. Tabs occupy3 cells. Supported CSI/OSC/APC sequences are removed before grapheme width calculation.

Grapheme width first counts terminal-spacing mark-only clusters, then zeroes clusters composed entirely of default-ignorable/control/mark/surrogate code points. RGI emoji clusters are2 cells, and isolated regional indicators U+1F1E6..1F1FF are conservatively2 even before a complete flag arrives. Other clusters use the first visible base's east-Asian width plus terminal-spacing marks and selected trailing visible code points after marks, half/fullwidth forms and Thai/Lao AM vowels. The exact mark exceptions are in utils.ts40–48 and must be kept as data, not approximated by scalar summation. Tests cover Indic conjuncts, Myanmar, combining marks, CJK and flag intermediates.

getGraphemeCellRange returns the whole nonzero-width grapheme cell interval containing a column, including the second cell of a wide glyph. normalizeTerminalOutput decomposes Thai U+0E33 to U+0E4D U+0E32 and Lao U+0EB3 to U+0ECD U+0EB2 throughout its input, then expands visible tabs to3 spaces while leaving tabs inside recognized terminal sequences intact. It does not rewrite logical editor content. The Thai/Lao replacement happens before terminal-sequence parsing, so unlike tabs it is not restricted to visible text.
entries.interfaces: getGraphemeSegmenter,getWordSegmenter,visibleWidth,getGraphemeCellRange,normalizeTerminalOutput; cjkBreakRegex identifies Han/Hiragana/Katakana/Hangul/Bopomofo. Integer cell positions differ from UTF-16 source offsets and Rust byte offsets.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:9-67 counts UnicodeWidthStr per scalar and skips controls/tabs unless an OSC/APC prefix triggers delegation to ansi.rs. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:15-87 measures the whole stripped string with UnicodeWidthStr. Those two public width paths can disagree on multi-scalar emoji, and neither applies the TS tab/spacing-mark/output-normalization contract. ansi.rs:135-142 only appends SGR0 when needed. utils.rs:354-377 exposes a grapheme wrapper whose index is an ordinal from enumerate(), unlike Intl's UTF-16 offset. Native general stripping recognizes more protocols than TS and should be preserved.
entries.port: Consolidate crates/ice-tui cell measurement around unicode-segmentation plus explicit terminal-width policy, keeping byte/UTF-16/cell coordinates distinct at boundaries. Add the fixed tab policy, mark exceptions and output-only Thai/Lao normalization to the terminal writer; retain native broad protocol stripping and test it separately. Use read TS fixtures as acceptance cases, not a scalar-width proxy.
entries.priority_reason: Visible behavior shared by terminal consumers must agree before higher-level component parity is reliable.

entries.title: ANSI-aware word wrapping and stable style carry across rows
entries.what: Wrap readable words and CJK graphemes without losing active styling or hyperlink clickability across logical and physical line breaks.
entries.mechanism:
TS extractAnsiCode recognizes CSI by scanning to m/G/K/H/J, OSC by BEL/ST, and APC by BEL/ST; unrecognized/incomplete sequences return null. This is deliberately narrower than a general terminal parser and can scan beyond an unsupported CSI final byte until a later accepted letter. Preserve native general parsing rather than reproducing that limitation silently.

AnsiCodeTracker separately tracks bold,dim,italic,underline,blink,inverse,hidden,strike,foreground/background and active OSC8 link including params and original BEL/ST terminator. Empty/0 SGR resets styling but not the link. It understands selective resets,8/16-color,256-color and RGB38/48;2;r;g;b with5 consumed parameters. Logical CRLF/CR/LF lines inherit active codes. Tokens keep ANSI attached to following visible content; literal spaces form whitespace runs and CJK-script graphemes are independent break opportunities. Overflow trims trailing whitespace, suppresses whitespace at a new line, and breaks a long token at grapheme boundaries.

A wrapped nonfinal line closes underline and an active hyperlink, reopens active codes on continuation, and intentionally leaves background/other styles for caller padding. Final segments do not receive an automatic full reset. A whole input line that already fits is returned as-is. Empty input yields one empty line. TS has no explicit nonpositive-width guard here: an indivisible grapheme wider than the requested width may produce an empty prefix then an overwide grapheme, so the documented universal <=width claim has that boundary limitation.
entries.interfaces: wrapTextWithAnsi(text,width):string[]; internal AnsiCodeTracker/getLineEndReset and token/long-word helpers. Source line902's token assignment was transport-redacted; surrounding tokenization implementation and consuming loop were fully visible.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:275-351 hard-wraps scalar characters, keeps leading wrap spaces, drops tabs/CR/control characters, drops a trailing empty newline and returns one empty line for width0. It subsequently calls rust:crates/ice-tui/src/line_diff.rs:223-234 to isolate ANSI rows; therefore style carry is present, not wholly missing. That isolator appends full reset plus BEL OSC8 close on every parsed row and preserves supported SGR/OSC8 state. Exact defect in line_diff.rs:111-178: RGB checks index+5 and consumes6 parameters, but standard38/48;2;r;g;b has5; normal RGB state is interpreted as unrelated SGR fragments on the next row, while an extra following parameter can be absorbed. Bold anddim share one native Intensity slot. Native atoms/slice/patch correctly use graphemes and reject unsupported controls to a fallback.
entries.port: Implement token/CJK word wrapping in crates/ice-tui with the common width function and an explicit attribute/link state machine; retain the native row-isolation/column-patch approach while fixing RGB parameter cardinality and independent bold/dim state. Choose/document final reset and padding ownership to match TS visible output without regressing safe independent row repaint. Keep width0 and indivisible-wide-grapheme behavior explicit.

entries.title: Bounded column slicing, ellipsis truncation and background continuation
entries.what: Clip and composite text by terminal cells while keeping grapheme boundaries, inherited styles and pane backgrounds intact.
entries.mechanism:
truncateToWidth returns empty at maxWidth<=0, optionally pads empty/short input, and returns original input if it fits even when the ellipsis itself is wider than the target. Otherwise it preserves a contiguous grapheme prefix within maxWidth-minus-ellipsis-width; it never skips a wide grapheme and resumes later. An oversized ellipsis is itself clipped by whole grapheme. Truncated results put SGR0 before and after nonempty ellipsis, or once after an empty ellipsis, then optional spaces to exact width. Retained ANSI codes are emitted only when followed by retained visible content. Tabs count3; large-input scanning stops once overflow is established.

sliceWithWidth/sliceByColumn preserve sequences occurring in the selected span and replay pending prefix sequences at the first included grapheme. A glyph starting before startCol is excluded. strict=false may include a wide glyph extending past the right edge; strict=true excludes it. Return actual width separately and do not imply automatic padding. extractSegments takes beforeEnd,afterStart,afterLen and optional strictAfter; before is always boundary-strict, after inherits effective attributes/link through a pooled tracker, including changes hidden under the overlay.

applyBackgroundToLine pads only when content is short, then splits around SGRs that reset background (empty,0,49) and re-applies bgFn to each intervening span. It skips the parameter arguments of38/48 extended colors so palette0 or RGB component49 are not mistaken for resets. It does not truncate an already-overwide input.
entries.interfaces: truncateToWidth(text,maxWidth,ellipsis='...',pad=false); sliceByColumn(line,start,length,strict=false); sliceWithWidth=>{text,width}; extractSegments=>{before,beforeWidth,after,afterWidth}; applyBackgroundToLine(line,width,bgFn).
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:93-131 strips all ANSI despite its preserve_styles flag and includes an endpoint grapheme even if it exceeds requested width. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:71-155 slices scalar characters, preserves a raw pending escape history, may overrun wide boundaries and bases padding on total source column rather than selected width. utils.rs:159-224 returns an overwide suffix unchanged when target width saturates to0 and puts the suffix before its final reset; no pad option. utils.rs:444-453 pads and calls bg_fn once, so SGR49 inside a panel is not generically reopened. Native line_diff.rs:238-269 already provides a stricter grapheme/style-aware private slice that blanks intersected wide cells; retain and reuse it instead of declaring all native clipping absent.
entries.port: Unify crates/ice-tui clipping/compositing around grapheme atoms, explicit result cell counts and shared SGR/OSC8 context. Port contiguous-prefix truncation and bounded ellipsis, offer strict/non-strict slice contracts intentionally, and reapply generic background closures after true resets. Preserve the native clipped-wide-cell blanking mode where layout requires it; compatibility wrappers can expose TS's exclusion semantics.

entries.title: OSC8 hyperlink hit-testing, selective removal and hover styling
entries.what: Identify the hyperlink under a terminal cell and change its presentation without confusing OSC parameters, text or closing sequences.
entries.mechanism:
TS recognizes OSC8 open/close with arbitrary parameter text, URL following the second semicolon, and either BEL or ST terminator. getOsc8LinkAtColumn tracks open URL and clears it on an empty URL; it returns the active URL for any occupied cell of a grapheme, including its second wide cell, with tabs counted3. It ignores other recognized terminal sequences.

The shared rewrite routine visits visible runs with current link identity while preserving non-OSC8 controls. stripOsc8Links removes wrappers only for matching URLs, keeping text and styling; a closing sequence follows the link it closes. styleOsc8Link wraps each visible text run for the selected URL with caller-provided open/close sequences, so decoration is reapplied after intervening ANSI changes. This is link state/presentation, not URL authorization or process launching.
entries.interfaces: getOsc8LinkAtColumn(line,column):string|undefined; stripOsc8Links(line,predicate); styleOsc8Link(line,url,open,close). Only the hit-test helper is re-exported by the package index.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:384-440 has a public hit-test helper but parses the URL after the first semicolon of8;params;uri. A normal8;;https payload therefore returns ';https'; a close8;; stores ';' and never clears in_osc8. It tests col==column rather than the interval occupied by a wide grapheme. This is an exact public-library behavior, not an observed browser launch: bounded crates search found only its definition and the lib.rs re-export, no internal interactive caller. Native line_diff.rs:181-197 parses and closes OSC8 correctly for row carry, so the defect is localized to this helper. No equivalent selective wrapper-removal/style-rewrite helper was established in the fully read native utility modules.
entries.port: Reuse a correct shared OSC8 decoder in crates/ice-tui, clear close state and test cell containment. Add selective rewrite helpers preserving BEL/ST and other controls; do not add external navigation as part of these pure operations. Keep native line-diff link parsing aligned with the same representation.

entries.title: Padded Text, Box, Spacer and first-line truncated components
entries.what: Render reusable text/padding containers with matching empty-content behavior, width accounting, backgrounds and cache invalidation.
entries.mechanism:
Text defaults text='',paddingX=1,paddingY=1,optional custom background. Raw empty or trim-empty text renders no rows. It expands every tab to3 spaces before wrapping, uses max(1,width-2*paddingX), surrounds each wrapped row with both horizontal margins and pads to width, then adds width-filled top/bottom rows. An optional bgFn applies through background-reset-aware utility. Its cache keys text and width; setText,setCustomBgFn and invalidate clear it. Caller-owned mutable background closures require invalidation if behavior changes without the setter.

Box defaults padding1/1, returns no rows for no children or all-empty child output, renders children at max(1,width-2*paddingX), prepends left padding then pads/backgrounds each row. Cache compares width, exact rendered child lines and bgFn('test') sample; it still renders children before cache lookup. setBgFn relies on sampling rather than immediate invalidation; invalidate cascades. removeChild removes only the first identity match. There is no intrinsic border in Box.

Spacer defaults1 empty row and supports setLines; it is unpadded and uncached. TruncatedText defaults zero margins, selects text before the first LF only, truncates at max(1,width-2*paddingX), surrounds/pads to full width and adds width-filled vertical rows. Empty text still renders one padded content row. These minimum-content-width policies can exceed an extremely narrow outer width when margins alone do not fit; do not claim hard clipping universally.

The unpadded Container exposes a mutable children array; addChild appends, removeChild deletes the first identity match, clear replaces the array, render concatenates every child at the same width, and invalidate calls optional child invalidation. It adds no layout sizing or implicit redraw.
entries.interfaces: Text(text='',paddingX=1,paddingY=1,bgFn?),setText,setCustomBgFn,invalidate; Box(addChild/removeChild/clear/setBgFn); Spacer(lines=1).setLines; TruncatedText(text,paddingX=0,paddingY=0). Container.children/addChild/removeChild/clear/render/invalidate.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/text.rs:28-125 has a content/width/theme-revision cache and setter, but subtracts only one horizontal padding, prefixes left padding only, emits empty unpadded vertical rows, does not suppress whitespace-only text or support custom background, and iterates str.lines before scalar wrapping. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/box_component.rs:29-208 largely mirrors caching/background sampling, but content width can be0 and remove_child removes every pointer-equal duplicate. Background behavior differs through utils. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/spacer.rs:12-31 renders the requested empty rows but has no mutator/default constructor. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/truncated_text.rs:19-92 instead stores a fixed max_width/custom ellipsis/style, renders min(max_width,viewport), does not select only the first logical line or add margins/padding. Preserve its useful native setters/custom ellipsis while adding the TS component contract. Native inline tests were fully read, not run. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/container.rs:16-82 supplies Arc-shared child storage, append/clear and ordered rendering, but removes every pointer-equal duplicate and holds the child mutex while calling render/invalidate. Retain owned child snapshots and avoid reentrant callback deadlock when adapting mutable component trees.
entries.port: Adjust crates/ice-tui components and compatibility constructors to expose paired margins, explicit blank behavior and optional background closures. Retain native theme-revision cache invalidation and existing custom-ellipsis/style controls. Share corrected wrap/clip/background helpers, avoid duplicating style state, and keep narrow-width margin behavior deliberate.

entries.title: Legacy, Kitty and modifyOtherKeys key identity and printable decoding
entries.what: Give raw terminal sequence consumers consistent logical key names, modifier matching and printable text without confusing keyboard layout, key release or protocol modes.
entries.mechanism:
TS uses Shift=1, Alt=2, Ctrl=4, Super=8 and masks CapsLock64/NumLock128. Kitty encoded modifiers are one-indexed; CSI-u accepts alternate shifted/base-layout codepoints and press/repeat/release event fields, with modified arrows/Home/End/tilde navigation. Keypad57399–57408 maps to0–9,57409–57413 to ./ * - + (57410 is slash),57415='=',57416=',',57417–57426 to navigation/delete;57414 is keypad Enter. Shifted uppercase Latin identity normalizes to lowercase. Latin letters/digits/known symbols remain authoritative over physical base-layout keys; other layouts can use reported base key. Legacy CSI/SS3/Linux/rxvt navigation/function-key sequences are enumerated at keys.ts368–480, including shifted lowercase CSI and Ctrl lowercase SS3, $/^ tilde variants, Alt-b/f/p/n arrows and F1–F12. Function-key matches only permit no modifiers.

Explicit Kitty and xterm CSI27;mod;code~ matching works regardless of negotiated mode. Ambiguous legacy Alt printable/control forms are disabled in Kitty mode; LF and ESC+CR become Shift+Enter there, otherwise Enter/Alt+Enter. Raw CR remains Enter; keypad SS3 OM is Enter. Local WT_SESSION without truthy SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT/SSH_TTY makes raw BS0x08 Ctrl+Backspace; DEL remains Backspace, and raw BS also matches Ctrl+h through the general raw-control path. Esc/return aliases and order-independent modifier strings match; parseKey emits modifiers in Shift,Ctrl,Alt,Super order, although raw uppercase ASCII parses as the uppercase character rather than the explicit shifted form. Unsupported modifier bits reject formatted key IDs.

isKeyRelease/isKeyRepeat scan supported :3/:2 suffix substrings (u,~,A–D,H,F), not a fully anchored event parser, and exempt bracketed-paste payloads. matchesKey does not itself suppress release events. decodeKittyPrintable permits only Shift and lock bits, prefers the reported shifted key, normalizes keypad keys, rejects controls/invalid codepoints, and returns String.fromCodePoint; it does not check the event-type field, so callers must discard releases where required. decodePrintableKey adds modifyOtherKeys with the same non-Control/Alt/Super printable policy.
entries.interfaces: KeyId/Key helper permutations; matchesKey,parseKey,isKeyRelease,isKeyRepeat,decodeKittyPrintable,decodePrintableKey,setKittyProtocolActive,isKittyProtocolActive. Raw strings and Crossterm structured events need an explicit adapter, not interchangeable representations.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/keys.rs:1-524 has a public string parser, but uses Ctrl=1/Shift=2/Alt=4, fails to subtract1, discards colon-containing parameters via filter_map and derives event type from the first keycode parameter. It misidentifies1~ as F1, groups several F-key numbers together, maps keypad57399 to Insert/57414 to Delete, omits alternate-layout/modifyOtherKeys/lock handling and accepts only ASCII printables. Key::to_key_id alphabetically sorts modifier names and exact-matches strings, conflicting with ctrl_alt helper order; global Kitty state does not affect parsing. Its printable decoder accepts ASCII CSI-u without checking modifiers or release type. These are source-established public-helper defects, not evidence all native typing is broken: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal.rs:401-415 supplies Crossterm KeyEvent, and keybindings.rs:686-703 matches those directly. Bounded crates search found no call to decode_kitty_printable_from_str beyond its definition.
entries.port: Implement a single protocol parser with correctly normalized flags, event types and keypad mappings; keep raw printable decoding separate from shortcut identity. Bridge native structured events while retaining Crossterm's direct Unicode input path. Add table-driven acceptance cases from the read TS tests plus malformed/locked/released events; do not enable modifyOtherKeys until the active input reader can decode it. Preserve the observed TS caller-level release policy rather than claiming its printable helper suppresses releases.
entries.priority_reason: Raw-input extensions and compatibility paths need correct key identity; active native structured-event handling must remain intact.

entries.title: Incremental sequence framing and bracketed-paste assembly
entries.what: Deliver complete escape events and paste payloads across arbitrary stdin chunks while keeping ordinary input responsive.
entries.mechanism:
StdinBuffer emits individual data sequences immediately and retains incomplete CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/SS3/meta sequences behind a resettable10ms default timer. CSI ends at a final byte0x40–0x7e; SGR mouse requires three numeric fields, old X10 mouse consumes ESC[M plus3 code units; OSC accepts BEL/ST, DCS/APC ST. Lone ESC flushes as one unfinished sequence. Explicit flush returns buffered data without emitting, clears the timer and pending printable marker; clear/destroy discard buffer,paste state and timers. Empty input emits an empty data event when ordinary buffer is empty. A single Buffer byte>127 converts to ESC+(byte−128); other buffers use toString.

Bracketed paste recognizes ESC[200~ and collects through ESC[201~, including split markers while the ordinary10ms fragment budget has not expired; paste-mode buffering has no timeout/cap. Input before a paste is parsed and emitted, content is one paste event, suffix recursively processes; an incomplete pre-paste remainder is discarded by that branch. TS ProcessTerminal re-wraps the payload for existing editors. Ordinary text splitting uses UTF-16 code units, not graphemes, so this source does not guarantee one event per supplementary Unicode scalar. A raw ESC followed by a second ESC introducing [/] /O/P/_ emits a standalone first ESC to avoid WezTerm Escape-release suffix leakage. After an unmodified no-semicolon Kitty printable report, one immediately following matching single-code-unit raw character is suppressed, including across chunks; intervening sequences/paste/clear reset the marker. This is narrow duplicate-text suppression, not generic event deduplication.
entries.interfaces: StdinBuffer({timeout?}), process(string|Buffer), data/paste event listeners, flush():string[],clear,getBuffer,destroy. Preserve order and distinguish timer disposal from incomplete paste policy.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/stdin_buffer.rs:1-312 is a batch queue/callback abstraction, not a protocol framer. It searches paste markers only inside each input argument, so a marker split between calls is missed (split end stays permanently inside paste). No partial-escape parser/timer/duplicate-text suppression exists. process updates last_input immediately before should_batch; its usual elapsed<1ms branch emits the entire input chunk as Data, not individual sequences. Batching only occurs if that same call takes1ms to less than16ms before checking, and there is no timer-driven flush. A single oversized chunk can exceed the nominal64KiB buffer cap. Callbacks run under the callback mutex and, on some paths, buffer/paste-buffer locks, making reentrant on_event/flush/reset calls capable of deadlock. The bounded crates search found StdinBuffer construction only in its inline tests; primary terminal.rs uses Crossterm instead. Native windows_paste.rs:22-119 separately bulk-reads up to1024 safe console records for a sole reader, preserves UTF-16 pairs and trailing Enter, and must not be removed.
entries.port: Provide the source-compatible incremental framer only at raw-stream boundaries, with callback dispatch outside locks and owned cancellable timers. Retain native structured-event and Windows bulk-paste paths; explicitly document which host owns each stream. Preserve TS observable assembly/dedup rules and document its UTF-16/timeout/unclosed-paste limits rather than attributing stronger behavior. Fixture tests should split every marker and protocol response at each boundary and verify one ordered payload without executing real terminal state.
entries.priority_reason: Fragmented input must not become commands or literal escape suffixes; the current native helper's name masks a materially different contract.

entries.title: Keyboard negotiation, platform modifier helpers and fallback input
entries.what: Negotiate enhanced keys without swallowing user input and restore terminal protocol state across start, drain and stop.
entries.mechanism:
TS starts raw UTF-8 stdin, enables bracketed paste, installs resize before Unix self-SIGWINCH, and enables Windows VT input after raw-mode setup. It pushes Kitty flags7, queries flags, and appends a device-attributes sentinel (ESC[>7u ESC[?u ESC[c). Nonzero flags activate global/terminal Kitty state and disable modifyOtherKeys; zero flags or DA before Kitty enables xterm modifyOtherKeys level2. There is no fixed whole-negotiation startup timeout; ordinary input is forwarded meanwhile. An incomplete ESC[ or ESC[?digits; prefix flushed by StdinBuffer receives a separate150ms fragment timer; valid continuations are consumed, invalid/expired prefixes replay as input. Pushed state is recorded independently of observed support so stop/drain can pop once.

On darwin TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal, raw CR becomes CSI13;2u only when the local native shift helper reports true. Unlike Rust's guard, this TS check does not exclude SSH. The lazy Darwin helper caches success/failure, supports x64/arm64, probes module-parent/module/executable native/prebuilds locations, validates isModifierPressed and returns false on unavailable/error. C reads combined-session CGEventSourceFlagsState for shift/command/control/option via a N-API bridge. Windows x64/arm64 loader probes analogous3 paths and calls optional enableVirtualTerminalInput; the C implementation ORs0x0200 onto existing stdin console mode and returns a boolean. TS ignores the boolean and returns after the first successfully loaded module.
entries.interfaces: Terminal.start/kittyProtocolActive, ProcessTerminal.modifyOtherKeysActive; parseKeyboardProtocolNegotiationSequence; isAppleTerminalSession,normalizeAppleTerminalInput,isNativeModifierPressed. Env TERM_PROGRAM,SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT/SSH_TTY and platform/architecture have distinct source/native semantics.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal.rs:16-65,187-290,340-369,469-506 implements flags7 negotiation through Crossterm, caches detected support across resumes and skips unsupported modifyOtherKeys because Crossterm cannot parse it. Native ICE_KITTY_KEYBOARD forces legacy only for value'0' and otherwise enables; macOS Otty TERM_PROGRAM/TERM bypasses protocol to preserve IME, and unmodified local Apple Terminal Enter consults CoreGraphics only outside SSH. These native safeguards and direct Unicode input tests at terminal.rs614-669 are valuable existing behavior. No TS-style DA/prefix replay state machine, generic exported4-modifier helper or Windows N-API adapter is needed literally in Rust, but the compatibility APIs/fallback reader contract remain partial.
entries.port: Implement negotiation as an owned state machine tied to the selected raw or structured reader. Add late/split response handling and fallback decoding where raw compatibility is required; never enable an encoding the active reader cannot consume. Expose equivalent modifier-query capability behind cfg(platform) and keep native Otty/SSH/IME safeguards, documenting intentional differences from TS. Use static fixtures and mock-terminal acceptance tests for ordering and one-pop restoration; OS helper packaging belongs only where a JS bridge is still distributed.
entries.priority_reason: Protocol state and platform fallback determine whether Enter, modifiers and IME remain usable.

entries.title: Terminal shutdown, input draining, progress and output contract
entries.what: Keep terminal ownership explicit, prevent late input reaching the parent shell, and provide the same dimensions/progress/output behavior to TUI consumers.
entries.mechanism:
TS drainInput(maxMs=1000,idleMs=50) pops pushed/active Kitty first, disables modifyOtherKeys, clears negotiation fragments, temporarily removes the component input handler while stdin continues consuming, and exits at max or an idle interval; finally restores the previous handler. stop clears active progress, disables bracketed paste, restores keyboard protocols once, destroys framing timers, removes stdin/stdout listeners, pauses stdin, and restores the originally observed raw flag. Dimensions prefer stdout, then numeric COLUMNS/LINES, then80x24 via truthy fallback (no integer/positive validation). Title uses OSC0; movement is relative up/down; line/from-cursor/screen clears are explicit.

setProgress(true) writes OSC9;4;3 BEL immediately and keeps it alive every1000ms without starting duplicate intervals; false clears interval and writes OSC9;4;0 BEL, stop clears only an active interval. write(data) writes stdout then optionally synchronously appends the same bytes to ICE_TUI_WRITE_LOG. A directory value becomes tui-localdate-time-pid.log; otherwise the value is used as a file, and stat/append errors are ignored. Protocol/control methods mostly write stdout directly and therefore are not all captured by write logging. getTuiEnv is an exact process.env lookup, not a legacy PI alias resolver; normalizeCursorMarkers is an identity function and ICE_CURSOR_MARKER is APC ice:c BEL.
entries.interfaces: Terminal.drainInput,start,stop,write,columns,rows,moveBy,clearLine,clearFromCursor,clearScreen,setTitle,setProgress; ICE_TUI_WRITE_LOG,COLUMNS,LINES,ICE_CURSOR_MARKER. Native Terminal also has refresh_size,enter/exit_raw_mode,mouse,flush and capability info that must remain available.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal.rs:299-466 restores raw mode by unconditional disable rather than previous-state restoration and has no drain API/write-log/env-dimension fallback. Native set_progress emits OSC9;4;1;0 for active and9;4;0;0 for clear once, without TS's indeterminate state3/keepalive/stop reset. Its title uses OSC2. A concrete public-start lifecycle defect exists: start creates a separate local Arc<Mutex<bool>> at386, read only by the spawned thread393, while stop updates self.running432; no path sets the local flag false or joins the thread. Resize updates an independent info_clone rather than self.info; active renderer refresh_size can compensate. That public reader also explicitly discards Event::Paste415. Primary CLI call-site search shows start_readerless in interactive_tui.rs1507/tui_shell.rs85/resume_picker.rs111, so this defect is not attributed to those readerless paths. Native mouse tracking intentionally preserves macOS native selection by default.
entries.port: Give each terminal owner a cancellable/joinable reader handle or require readerless ownership; stop and drain must coordinate with the actual reader and restore prior raw/protocol/progress state exactly once. Implement compatible dimension and writer hooks, with the source's log scope documented. Retain native mouse/resize watchdog capabilities and separate main/alternate policies. Verify the public-start path with a fake event source and cancellation acknowledgments; do not infer runtime hangs from source-only inspection.
entries.priority_reason: Shutdown and input ownership affect shell recovery; source identifies a bounded public-reader cancellation defect.

entries.title: Generic keybinding registry, defaults and conflict semantics
entries.what: Share extensible action definitions and user overrides across editors, selectors and alternate-screen viewport controls without evicting valid defaults.
entries.mechanism:
TS accepts arbitrary definition maps with defaultKeys:string|string[] and optional descriptions; declaration merging extends the typed Keybindings interface. Per-action user keys replace that action only, undefined selects defaults, [] disables, and duplicate exact key strings are removed in first-occurrence order. Unknown user IDs are preserved in the user config snapshot but ignored for resolution/conflicts. Conflicts include only keys explicitly claimed by two or more recognized user actions; shared defaults and default-versus-user overlap are deliberately not conflicts and no action is evicted. entries.title: Stack allocation, visibility and direct rendering
entries.what: Allocate horizontal and vertical stack children deterministically under basis, grow, shrink, min/max, gap and viewport visibility constraints.
entries.mechanism:
Stack stores component entries in order; addChild normalizes finite numeric gap/grow/shrink/min/max to nonnegative floored integers (fallback gap/grow/min0,shrink1,max MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), while basis is retained and normalized by allocation. Defaults are basis auto,grow0,shrink1,min0,max unlimited,align stretch. visible(viewport) filters entries before gaps/allocation; direct render passes effectively unbounded viewport height, while constrained layout uses real dimensions. removeChild removes the first identity match from both child/entry lists; clear empties both.

allocateStackSizes clamps basis or measured intrinsic size to min and max adjusted to at least min. With an available size, subtract gaps and repeatedly distribute remaining growth/overflow among eligible children until exhausted/no progress. Grow weight is grow; shrink weight is shrink*max(1,currentSize). Each ordered candidate receives at least1 up to floor(currentRemaining*weight/totalWeight), capacity and remaining; remaining decreases inside the same pass. Recompute eligible weights on subsequent passes. Therefore this is an ordered iterative integer algorithm, not a single proportional division. Unsatisfied min constraints may still overflow.

Direct VStack renders children, applies natural basis/min/max sizes by slicing or blank-padding, and inserts gaps. HStack measures all visible children at outer width, allocates, re-renders each nonzero-width child at its own width, uses max rendered height and vertically offsets center/end children before ANSI-aware composition. Empty stacks render no rows.
entries.interfaces: StackChild,StackEntry,StackEntryOptions,StackOptions,Stack,HStack,VStack,visibleStackEntries,allocateStackSizes; basis:'auto'|number,grow,shrink,minSize,maxSize,visible, gap,align.

Entries expose no visibility closure and conversion forces visible=None; native layout_node.rs:82-237 separately defines visible fn pointers/default shrink1 but normal stack construction does not use them. Generic allocator uses single proportional passes, adds at most one leftover grow cell per entry and no shrink remainder pass; native actual constrained helper vstack.rs374-485 uses shrink factor without size weighting, also leaves capped leftovers, and basis.clamp panics if min>max. Direct VStack305-325 ignores basis/min/max entirely. Direct HStack110-230 renders only at outer width, has no shrink/visibility, horizontally aligns within allocated columns instead of TS vertical cross-axis alignment, returns one empty row for no children, and removes all duplicate pointers. Native constrained layout already recurses real stacks; retain that implementation rather than declaring layout absent.

Route direct HStack through allocated-width rendering and cross-axis positioning; preserve native convenience constructors/getters. Verify capped-growth redistribution, odd shrink remainders, min>max, zero width and nested intrinsic min constraints against source fixtures.

entries.title: Extensible constrained layout tree and nested scroll geometry
entries.what: Expose component layout nodes and produce one clipped geometry tree for rendering, cursor visibility and nested scroll hit routing.
entries.mechanism:
The symbol-based layout hook lets any component return vstack/hstack/scroll structure. A frame uses floor-normalized positive dimensions and a per-component/per-width render cache so measure and paint share results; fixed basis skips unnecessary intrinsic measurement. Leaves keep full rendered lines, allocate requested/natural height and shift lineOffset just far enough to keep their first cursor marker visible. VStack allocates each child vertically and computes natural height with gaps. HStack allocates widths, measures children at their own positive width, applies stretch/start/center/end vertical placement and represents zero-width children without painting.

Scroll layout recursively lays out the child at unbounded height and y−oldScrollTop, obtains actual constrained child geometry, updates state, translates descendants for the new scroll position and recalculates ancestor-intersected clips. Thus nested ScrollViews remain in the tree. Frame primary selection uses the first encountered scroll as fallback and replaces it whenever a later marked-primary scroll is encountered. getScrollViewBox searches by state identity; getScrollViewsAt returns containing clipped scrolls deepest-first. Every child has a real parent reference; coordinates may be negative for offscreen content.

Painting iterates only clipped visible row ranges, removes leading OSC133 A/B/C zone markers, composes at allocated x/width and handles Kitty top/bottom cropping through image metadata. The full-width painted-row cache keys line+width, scrollbar cache also sampled style; lines>4096 code units bypass, and cache clears when reaching4096 entries. Image-specific protocol/cropping details belong with terminal images.
entries.interfaces: LAYOUT_NODE,getLayoutNode,LayoutNode/StackLayoutNode/ScrollLayoutNode/LayoutViewport; LayoutRect,LayoutBox,LayoutFrame,renderLayoutFrame,getScrollViewBox,getScrollViewsAt. Custom layout hooks must not require concrete built-in downcasts.

It ignores the exported LayoutNodeProvider trait and recognizes only three concrete downcasts. VStack passes height.unwrap_or(0) to constrained allocation even for unbounded intrinsic layout. HStack ignores cross-axis align and omits zero-width boxes. ScrollView is flattened to pre-sliced lines with no child boxes/scroll_content_lines, so nested geometry/hit routing is lost. Only the first explicitly primary scroll is registered (no unmarked fallback). get_scroll_views_at at661-680 traverses outer-first; parent_index is populated with each child's own ordinal rather than a navigable parent, and unsigned coordinates cannot represent negative content origins. Paint504-548 copies full-width lines directly and has no source zone stripping, image crop or painted-row cache. Preserve native scroll-content reuse and cache tests at layout.rs868-979.

entries.title: Scroll state, follow-end and render notifications
entries.what: Make explicit and relative scrolling preserve follow-end state and report unused deltas consistently to nested viewport routing.
entries.mechanism:
ScrollView owns exactly one child; unsupported nonvertical axis throws and add/remove/clear throw explicit errors. Defaults are follow none,primary false,overscroll chain,scrollbar hidden. scrollTo truncates finite positions and otherwise keeps the current value, clamps to range, returns without changing follow state if position is unchanged, and notifies only on movement. scrollBy truncates finite delta, starts at current maximum when following end, updates position/follow state, emits render only when movement occurred and returns requested minus moved for chaining. scrollToStart restores follow only when configured end and content fits; scrollToEnd restores configured follow even if the position already equals end. Both notify only for actual position/follow changes.

updateLayout floors nonnegative content/viewport heights, installs requestRender, sticks to max while following, clamps while detached and automatically restores follow if configured end and clamping reaches the end; content fitting hides transient bars. Direct render is unscrolled full child content, with one appended space per row if always-scrollbar reserves a column. Constrained rendering owns the viewport, not this direct render method.
entries.interfaces: ScrollViewOptions axis,follow,primary,overscroll; scrollTop,isFollowingEnd,viewportHeight,scrollTo,scrollBy,scrollToStart,scrollToEnd,updateLayout,getContentWidth; exactly-one-child invariant.

Native scroll_by222-260 never invokes request_render; scroll_to/start/end always invoke it even for no-op, and normal layout invokes update_layout(...,None), leaving callback unset unless a caller installs it separately. Options are immutable; no overscroll accessor/routing is exposed here. Direct render465-470 reduces width for Always but does not append a reserved-column space. Native preserve_manual_position prevents reattaching follow when resize makes content temporarily fit, a deliberate useful extension documented by tests634-655; preserve it instead of forcing TS semantics globally. The single private child field enforces one-child ownership without TS mutation errors.

Install render callbacks when binding layout, notify on actual moves/state changes, return chain deltas unchanged and reserve direct-render width consistently. Specify no-op scrollTo follow behavior separately from explicit start/end. Keep renderer-owned cached viewports and test resize/shrink/append/manual-return state transitions.
entries.priority_reason: Follow state and callback timing determine whether users keep their browsing position during streaming.

entries.title: Transient scrollbars, proportional geometry and cell-preserving style
entries.what: Show configurable scrollbar feedback without erasing the transcript glyph under an automatic overlay scrollbar.
entries.mechanism:
Hidden never shows; Always shows for a positive viewport and reserves one column only if width>1; Auto appears transiently only when content overflows and user scrolling marks activity. Layout-driven follow advancement does not flash it. Activity restarts an unref'd hide timer (default1000ms, floored/nonnegative), except while scrollbarActive is held; releasing active starts the timer. Changing scrollbar mode requests render and hides transient state outside Auto. Track style is optional/mutable; thumb style defaults SGR100 background then49 reset, and both closures may resolve current theme at call time.

Geometry uses the rightmost column, full viewport track, minimum thumb min(2,height), rounded height²/contentHeight capped to track, and rounded scroll fraction over max thumb offset. Style the complete grapheme containing that column, including both cells of a CJK glyph, by preserving its text and leading escape context then wrapping the target in the selected style. Fill a missing cell with space, skip image lines, leave nonthumb track untouched when no track style, and clip vertical and horizontal painting. Cache keys include style(' ') so changed closure output invalidates the painted row.
entries.interfaces: ScrollViewScrollbar,setScrollbar,setScrollbarActive,isScrollbarVisible,set/getScrollbarTrackStyle,getScrollbarGeometry,ScrollbarGeometry; thumb/track styling closures and scrollbarHideDelayMs.

There is no active/hover lifetime, mode setter or custom track/thumb closure. Thumb size is floored with minimum1 and position floored. It replaces the rightmost cell with a styled space for thumb and a plain space for track, erasing transcript content in Auto instead of tinting the containing grapheme. Built-in image escape checks avoid painting two supported image forms, but there is no exposed geometry for dragging. Main theme/appearance adapters remain in the coordinator's TUI entries.

Share geometry among painter and mouse drag handler; retain native image skips and ensure automatic bars consume no layout width. entries.title: ANSI-safe row composition, blank clearing and image protection
entries.what: Composite overlays and horizontal children into fixed terminal cells while preserving surrounding styles and preventing graphics bytes from being sliced as text.
entries.mechanism:
compositeTuiLine immediately preserves an image-bearing base row. For text, it extracts before/after base segments with tracked ANSI/OSC8 context, slices the overlay strictly to its allocated width, fills any wide-cell boundary holes and short spans with spaces, inserts SGR0+OSC8-close between before/overlay/after and pads to total width. An empty overlay still clears its allocated span. The final result is strictly clipped if wider than the viewport. Overlay width/start are allocated by the caller; this helper does not independently interpret positioning percentages or focus.

Layout's full-width fast path still passes ordinary text through composition and only directly assigns full-width image lines. A scrollbar may restyle a whole wide glyph rather than replace a partial cell. These rules make clearing blank panel rows and protecting image data separate from ordinary overlay placement.
entries.interfaces: compositeTuiLine(baseLine,overlayLine,startCol,overlayWidth,totalWidth); SEGMENT_RESET; callers include HStack/layout/overlay painters. Common cell segmentation and terminal-image classification are prerequisites.

It returns the base unchanged when overlay visible width is0, so an empty allocated panel span does not clear. It has no image-base guard, calculates the retained after region to the full base end rather than the viewport end, and lacks final width clipping, so an overlong base can keep excess suffix cells. Its full-width layout paint copies lines without this guard. Native render.rs:52-94 exposes a second scalar-character compositor that counts ANSI bytes as characters and does not enforce width; retain neither as an undocumented substitute for the main composer. The native line_diff RGB carry defect is separately owned by TUI-202.

entries.priority_reason: Blank clearing and style isolation are required for reliable overlays and nested panels.

entries.title: Renderer lifecycle, frame scheduling and restart ownership
entries.what: Coalesce component invalidations into paced frames while preserving forced redraw, start/stop order, and correct ownership of terminal resources.
entries.mechanism: TuiBase starts with stopped=false/running=false. start clears stopped, runs beforeTerminalStart, installs terminal input/resize callbacks, runs afterTerminalStart, hides cursor, optionally enables color notifications, queries cell size for image-capable terminals, and requests rendering. stop marks stopped/running first, cancels pending render timeout, disables requested notifications, runs before-stop hook, restores cursor/terminal and after-stop hook. Normal requestRender coalesces through nextTick plus a 16ms minimum frame interval measured with performance.now; requests raised while painting cause another schedule. Force resets subclass render state and queues nextTick while bypassing the interval. renderNow cancels pending work, resets state only when forced, updates timestamp, and paints immediately; subclasses guard stopped state. Restart can install fresh scheduling after stop. clearOnShrink defaults true unless ICE_CLEAR_ON_SHRINK='0'; hardware cursor defaults false unless ICE_HARDWARE_CURSOR='1', with explicit constructor option taking precedence. Changing hardware cursor immediately hides it if disabling and requests a frame.

Force renders synchronously; normal requests require running and can be host-flushed or scheduler-driven. start_render_scheduler records scheduler_started, but stop_render_scheduler sets shutdown and joins without clearing scheduler_started or resetting shutdown: restarting this same scheduled TuiAltScreen cannot start another scheduler and subsequent normal requests park without a worker. Inline initial render still occurs, so this is a restart-specific source defect, not failure of first start. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tui_alt_screen.rs:1079-1349 defaults clear_on_shrink=false, setters only store, and invalidate omits overlays. The distinct rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tui_main_screen.rs:143-187 immediately rerenders even when stopped and request_render discards force. Preserve native scheduler merge priority, readerless CLI mode, resize watchdog and foreign-runtime suspension rather than replacing them wholesale.

Align settings defaults and setter invalidation. Unify public regular-mode scheduling with the active renderer and ensure overlay caches are invalidated. Keep synchronous native flush as an explicit API while exposing TS-compatible queued force semantics where needed.

entries.title: Input interception, focusable delivery and hardware cursor markers
entries.what: Deliver framed input through ordered interception and current focus, consume terminal replies, and place the hardware cursor without leaking markers into terminal output.
entries.mechanism: Input order is pending OSC11 reply, color-scheme report, registered input listeners in insertion order, cell-size response, debug Ctrl+Shift+D, focus visibility/restore maintenance, then the focused component. A listener may consume, replace data, or replace it with empty data to stop processing. Input reaches components including Ctrl+C; key releases are withheld unless wantsKeyRelease===true. No generic keybinding layer consumes text at TuiBase. Positive CSI 6;height;width t updates global cell dimensions, invalidates mounted roots and every overlay, and requests rendering; nonpositive matching replies are consumed without state update. Focusability is structural via a focused property. Global frame line finalization normalizes legacy markers and appends SGR0 plus OSC8 close to each nonimage line. Cursor extraction scans bottom-up only within the terminal viewport, selects the first marker in the winning line and removes that marker; other markers are not globally removed by this helper. Main-screen cursor uses absolute column G and tracked row delta, hides when absent, and honors hardware visibility; alternate screen positions by absolute row/column and explicitly emits show or hide each frame.

Native alternate renderer at 908-1054 removes every cursor marker (retain this stronger hygiene), but set_show_hardware_cursor(false) does not hide/request and a marker with disabled visibility emits no hide. Native regular renderer at 663-906 scans cursor markers outside viewport and unconditionally shows a found cursor, ignoring hardware visibility. Native general frame path lacks TS line normalization/reset closure and terminal-reply/listener pipeline.

Share viewport-bound cursor extraction while retaining all-marker stripping. Ensure show/hide policy is enforced on both frame modes and append closure only to ordinary text lines.

entries.title: Overlay focus stack, hidden-state transitions and deferred restoration
entries.what: Maintain independent overlay membership, paint order, focus ownership and restoration so nested or temporarily hidden overlays do not steal focus from explicit caller targets.
entries.mechanism:
showOverlay captures preFocus, assigns a monotonically increasing focusOrder and appends membership. Visible capturing overlays take focus; nonCapturing overlays may still be explicitly focused. Hide permanently removes membership, retargets other entries' preFocus links that pointed to it, and if focused restores the highest focusOrder visible capturing overlay or its prior target. hideOverlay removes the last inserted entry, not the latest focused entry. setHidden is a reversible visibility flag; hiding restores focus and clears restore state, showing a visible capturing entry raises focusOrder and focuses. handle.focus checks membership and visibility, raises order, then focuses. hasOverlay uses current terminal-size visibility predicate; raw hasOverlayEntries includes hidden entries. All entries are invalidated including hidden ones.

Focus restoration has explicit eligible/blocked states. Moving from an eligible overlay to a target outside its preFocus ancestor chain blocks restoration on that target. A later explicit focus operation may carry or resolve the blocked state; unmounting the blocker allows restoration. handle.unfocus({target}) supports explicit target including null, and can store a deferred target while another blocker remains focused. Unfocus without target clears its restore claim. Structural focused flags are toggled for previous/new focusable components. The restoration graph and membership traversal, rather than simply popping a stack, determine behavior.

Source-read regression matrix: ice:packages/tui/test/overlay-non-capturing.test.ts:55-1203 exercises explicit/null unfocus targets, blockers that move focus or unmount, invisible-but-eligible overlays, cycle prevention, handle no-op guards and visual order separate from membership. Tests were read, not executed.
entries.interfaces: OverlayHandle.hide,setHidden,isHidden,focus,unfocus({target?:Component|null}),isFocused; OverlayOptions.nonCapturing,visible; Component focus and mounted-root contract.

New handles report focused=true without changing TUI focus; focus only sets that local flag, never clears siblings, and hide/set_hidden do not request a redraw. No unfocus, preFocus retargeting or deferred restoration exists. has_overlay checks manager visible flags but not size-dependent predicate used at render time. Invalidation visits base roots without overlay components.

Add an explicit restoration state machine and target graph matching the source transitions; avoid deadlocking component callbacks under manager locks. Preserve native Arc ownership and passive-overlay placement as separate concerns.

entries.title: Overlay size resolution, screen anchoring and passive placement
entries.what: Resolve overlay width/height/position deterministically against the viewport and composite visible overlays in focus order without retaining stale document high-water rows.
entries.mechanism:
Margins may be one number or four edges, each clamped nonnegative. Available dimensions are at least1. Numeric width is used directly; a valid nonnegative decimal percentage is floored against full terminal width. Default width=min(80,availableWidth). minWidth is applied before clamping into1..availableWidth. maxHeight is optional, numeric or percentage of full terminal height and clamped1..availableHeight; absent maxHeight does not clip content to the viewport. Render occurs once at resolved width, maxHeight clips only when supplied, then final position uses actual rendered height. Explicit numeric row/col or percentages position within free remaining extent plus margins; invalid percentage falls back to centered. Nine anchors are the alternative, followed by offsets and margin clamps.

Visible entries paint ascending focusOrder. Composite working height is max(current base rows,terminal rows,row+overlay rows), never historical maxLinesRendered; overlays address that resulting viewport. Blank overlay rows clear their allocated span through the compositor. This means presence of hidden entries can still cause the caller to enter overlay composition, but only visible entries render. TS allows passive/nonCapturing overlays to overlap; it is solely a focus policy.

Source-read geometry checks at ice:packages/tui/test/overlay-options.test.ts:173-540 pin percentage widths/minWidth, margin clamps, anchor/absolute precedence, optional clipping and stacked paint order. Earlier overflow cases mostly assert no crash/visible content, not exact cell output; the exact CJK boundary assertions are ice:packages/tui/test/regression-overlay-cjk-boundary.test.ts:6-46.

Native Percent is a fractional value rounded against terminal size, so representation and rounding differ. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/overlay.rs:21-97 defaults width to all available width then shrinks to rendered text width if width omitted; defaults max height to available and clips every overlay; zero/empty geometry is dropped. A visibility fn pointer cannot capture environment. Manager render_visible at 178-248 preserves insertion/z order and additionally shifts passive overlays vertically to avoid prior passive overlays with a row gap, omitting those that cannot fit. Keep that native useful policy explicitly configurable, rather than silently claiming TS parity.

Route both native modes through one ordered screen compositor. Keep passive collision avoidance as an opt-in/native policy distinct from noncapturing focus behavior.
entries.priority_reason: Geometry differences directly affect extension dialogs, previews and overlays near narrow or short viewport edges.

entries.title: Terminal background queries and color-scheme reply ownership
entries.what: Parse terminal color replies with exact framing and ensure asynchronous requests, late replies and scheme notifications cannot leak response bytes into editor input.
entries.mechanism: OSC11 must be exactly ESC]11;body followed by BEL or ST. Body supports #RRGGBB or #RRRRGGGGBBBB and slash-separated rgb/rgba (prefix case-insensitive and optional); only first3 slash fields matter, each nonempty hexadecimal channel of arbitrary digit width scales and rounds to0..255. Scheme report is one or more concatenated CSI ?997;1n / ;2n, with only all-valid concatenations accepted and the last report deciding dark/light. queryBackgroundColor writes OSC11 and enqueues FIFO request records. A timeout resolves undefined but leaves its record and pending count so a late matching reply is swallowed against that record instead of resolving a newer request; no reply can therefore leave a timed-out record at the FIFO front indefinitely. Only replies while pending are intercepted; a matching malformed body still consumes and settles undefined. Scheme query subscribes once plus timeout then writes CSI ?996n; every matching report broadcasts to current subscriptions, including concurrent requests. Notification toggle uses CSI ?2031 h/l; received valid reports are recognized regardless of toggle. stop does not cancel outstanding color-query records/timers.
entries.interfaces: parseOsc11BackgroundColor(string)->RGB|undefined, parseTerminalColorSchemeReport->'dark'|'light'|undefined; queryBackgroundColor(timeoutMs?), queryColorScheme(timeoutMs?), onTerminalColorSchemeChange, setTerminalColorSchemeNotifications.

RgbColor::from_hex slices UTF-8 by byte offsets after length6 check, so certain non-ASCII length6 input can panic rather than return None; four-byte channel slicing has a similar boundary hazard. parse_terminal_color_scheme_report at198 always returns Some(default-or-collected palette), parses OSC10/11/12 and never the CSI997 preference protocol. query helpers only return strings; focused source search found exports/definitions, no runtime query consumer in crates. Preserve native foreground/cursor palette support and luminance helpers as additional APIs, not equivalent to dark/light notifications.

Implement FIFO late-reply ownership and timeout/subscription disposal in the event owner, documenting the source's missing-reply head-of-line behavior rather than silently dropping old records. Coordinate appearance consumers through TUI-007.

entries.title: Main-screen differential rendering, shrink policy and transcript cursor accounting
entries.what: Update only changed transcript rows while preserving terminal scrollback, handling viewport movement, overlays and image row reservations.
entries.mechanism:
The renderer tracks previous lines/dimensions, logical content end, actual hardware row, viewport top and maximum rows rendered. It renders base, composites overlays, extracts viewport cursor and closes ordinary line styles. Initial full paint does not clear; width change always clears screen+scrollback; height change does so except TERMUX_VERSION; clearOnShrink triggers when new length is below historical maximum and there are no overlay entries. Full paint clips overwide ordinary text and uses Kitty reservation rows so image transmission does not scroll unexpectedly. Differential comparison expands changed ranges to affected old/new image blocks, deletes changed old image IDs, and repaints only first..last changed rows. Changes above previously visible rows or deletion that would move above viewport force clear/full paint. Pure deletion clears rows without scrolling when possible. Appending starts with CRLF after old content and advances viewport bookkeeping. In-viewport overlay changes use absolute screen rows to avoid relative drift. A differential ordinary line wider than terminal causes a crash log, terminal stop, then error; full paints clip instead. Debug-redraw and render dumps are opt-in and file failures are not caught.

captureRenderState copies text/dimensions/cursor/high-water state; restore blanks image lines and clears tracked image IDs. Normal stop moves to logical end and writes newline, unless preserveScreen or there was no history. No-change frames still reposition/hide/show cursor. Full-redraw counter increments only actual full paints.

Source-read test coverage includes image pre-clear/full-redraw ordering and taller-than-viewport fallback at ice:packages/tui/test/tui-render.test.ts:100-348, Termux height behavior at350-405, default shrink and stale high-water cleanup at430-807, absolute in-viewport overlay updates at ice:packages/tui/test/overlay-screen-position.test.ts:12-57, and line-style isolation at ice:packages/tui/test/tui-overlay-style-leak.test.ts:52-81. These tests are evidence of intended contracts, not executed results.

entries.title: Alternate-screen frame assembly, teardown transcript and mode ownership
entries.what: Render a viewport-owned application frame and leave a readable transcript when exiting fullscreen while restoring terminal and image capability state.
entries.mechanism:
Without explicit layout root, TuiAltScreen wraps normal children in an implicit primary ScrollView with follow=end. setLayoutRoot identity changes clear cached layout and request a frame. Start clears selection/drag/flash timers and image upload cache, captures image protocol, temporarily disables iTerm2 images globally and invalidates if needed, resets render state, enters alternate screen, disables autowrap and enables requested mouse/focus modes before terminal keyboard setup. Each frame clamps width/height to at least1, lays out root, strips leading OSC133 A/B/C zones, composites overlays, keeps last viewport-height rows, applies selection/action hover/flash, extracts cursor, closes nonimage styles and clips ordinary overwide rows. Full repaint occurs on first frame or dimension change; synchronized output wraps clearing, image actions, changed rows and explicit cursor visibility. Normal nonimage unchanged rows are skipped; any image change repaints all rows.

Stop first cancels selection/scrollbar/flash state, deletes Kitty images, disables mouse and reenables autowrap on the owning alternate screen, then terminal.stop disables keyboard there. After leaving the screen, preserveScreen only restores the original screen. Otherwise source rerenders the full document, strips cursor/leading zones, normalizes/clips rows and appends them to the restored main screen with per-line clearing, final reset/newline and cursor show. Temporarily disabled iTerm2 capability is then restored.

Source-read integration checks at ice:packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts:39-449 cover implicit and explicit scroll roots, dock stability, overlay invalidation, wheel routing, page overlap/modified key pass-through, semantic zones and iTerm fallback. Teardown ordering and full transcript restoration are asserted at893-927.

Its no-root fallback is plain container layout, not implicit primary scrolling. is_viewport_tui uses concrete TuiAltScreen type even if configured regular mode instead of a capability marker. entries.title: Viewport wheel routing, prompt navigation and scrollbar dragging
entries.what: Route viewport keyboard and mouse gestures to the correct nested scroll view, preserving overscroll policies and active scrollbar state.
entries.mechanism:
The viewport input listener consumes focus-in/out, wheel, SGR mouse and otherwise recognized mouse sequences before focused components. Focus-out cancels active press/autoscroll/drag/hover and clears in-progress selection, while an already completed selection remains. SGR wheel supports button64/65 (including modifier bits) and X10 six-character wheel frames; horizontal wheel codes are ignored as wheel, then mouse input is still swallowed. Wheel lines default1 and floor/clamp to at least1. Route deepest hit scroll views, pass unconsumed delta outward until zero or contain, then fall back to unseen primary if remainder remains; always request frame. Keyboard page movement uses max(1,viewportHeight-4), top/bottom and previous/next OSC133 A prompt row. Matching releases are consumed without movement.

Scrollbar hit tests only the thumb cell, disabled when any visible overlay exists. Hover toggles setScrollbarActive. Primary nonmotion press on thumb clears selection and records grabbed offset. Drag recomputes current geometry each event, clamps thumb offset and maps rounded fraction to max scrollTop; release stops drag. No track click behavior is implemented. Viewport key handling still runs through the listener even with overlays; it is not automatically suppressed by overlay focus.
entries.interfaces: TuiAltScreenOptions.wheelScrollLines,mouse; tui.altScreen.pageUp/pageDown/previousPrompt/nextPrompt/top/bottom bindings; SGR/X10 mouse protocol; getScrollViewsAt and ScrollView.overscroll.

Its public start discards events; readerless CLI host handles input separately. Native ScrollView overscroll and layout hit-test differences are recorded in TUI-212/213 rather than counted again. Application-specific CLI event integration remains a consumer dependency; this entry does not infer its total behavior from absence in the primitive. The host slice rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1752-1782 independently confirms side-question input and jump-to-end priority, then wheel scrolling of scroll_for_key directly with cached repaint only if position changes; a generic nested layout routing contract remains absent in the primitive. Native jump-to-end is fully verified at rust:crates/ice-tui/src/jump_to_end.rs:23-99: it paints only on a primary follow-end view currently scrolled away, suppresses under overlays/image/cursor rows, centers within clip while preserving scrollbar column and captures only left-button Down inside its last painted rect. Preserve this host-specific additional affordance.
entries.port: Implement reusable viewport event routing at the actual event owner, with normalized native mouse/key events and ownership boundaries for overlays and focus. Use layout hit-test/scroll contracts and expose consumed/remainder behavior to CLI; keep native cached-scroll repaint. Add source-compatible thumb activation and drag state, cancelling it on stop/focus loss.
entries.priority_reason: Nested scrolling and mouse ownership need an explicit shared contract before CLI gestures can match the source.

entries.title: Application text selection, OSC52 copy and internal hyperlink activation
entries.what: Select logical scroll content across viewport movement, copy only selected text, and distinguish an un-dragged hyperlink click from a selection gesture.
entries.mechanism:
Primary press records a point in deepest scroll content when there is no overlay, otherwise screen coordinates, and captures OSC8 URL from the displayed row. Motion only during active press marks dragged, cancels URL activation, updates focus point and enables50ms unref autoscroll when pointer reaches clipped top/bottom. Each tick moves one logical row, updates selection from current layout and stops at scroll boundary. Release requires the active press; same view,row,col without any drag activates the pressed URL via optional openUrl and catches callback errors. Otherwise copy uses ordered inclusive endpoints, whole-grapheme start/end cells, scrollContentLines when anchored in a scroll view, trims each selected row's trailing whitespace, strips terminal controls and writes OSC52 clipboard base64 only if nonempty, then flashes 'Copied!'. A point-only selection does not copy.

Highlight maps logical selection back through scroll offset and clip rectangle; image lines are skipped, ANSI-aware fragments preserve surrounding text, and reverse video is reasserted after every embedded SGR. Action URLs are classified by caller; their OSC8 wrappers are stripped only on terminal output while retained in previousScreen for hit tests. Hover highlights the URL only on pointer's row and only with no visible overlay, using a background style; it repaints only when entering/leaving the action link. Ordinary OSC8 URLs remain terminal-visible.

Source-read regression cases at ice:packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts:648-785 and810-872 cover action-URL hiding/hover, BEL/ST OSC8 clicks, no click on drag, OSC52 output, orphan drag/release suppression, focus-loss cancellation, edge autoscroll and CJK/emoji/combining boundary snapping.
entries.interfaces: TuiAltScreenOptions.openUrl(url),isActionUrl(url); OSC8 internal state vs serialized lines; OSC52 clipboard; flash(message); pointer/selection lifecycle.

Native editor selection is a separate text-editing feature, not transcript selection. A focused crates search found get_osc8_link_at_column only defined and exported, so its parser bug is not asserted to break an existing native click path. Native CLI may own other mouse routing; consumers must wire this new primitive through their actual event loop. Preserve existing native OSC8 rendering and explicit host URL policy rather than opening URLs directly from a rendering helper. Independently inspected rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1752-1850: the active host routes side-question mouse first, then jump-to-end indicator, primary transcript wheel, Windows right-click paste, and left press/drag/release selection. It stores screen cells, only copies after a real drag, reads fullscreen_copy_on_select live with true fallback, calls extract_selected_text(chat_container,start,end) and native clipboard, then clears selection. Expose clipboard/URL callbacks to the host and maintain separate logical-vs-terminal lines for action URLs. entries.title: Terminal image, color and hyperlink capability detection
entries.what: Expose a cached capability snapshot and independently mutable pixel cell dimensions that drive image rendering and hyperlink fallbacks.
entries.mechanism: Cell dimensions default to9x18 pixels and are set/get without validation; the capability cache is lazy and reset makes the next get redetect. Environment values are lowercased for terminal-name checks. TMUX or TERM starting tmux disables images and trusts only COLORTERM=truecolor/24bit for color; hyperlinks come from the injectable tmux probe. That probe synchronously runs tmux display-message -p '#{client_termfeatures}', splits comma features, recognizes hyperlinks and catches timeout/failure to false (250ms). TERM starting screen disables images and hyperlinks. Kitty, Ghostty (including GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR), WezTerm and Warp program/session markers enable Kitty images, truecolor and hyperlinks. iTerm program/session markers enable iTerm2. Windows Terminal, VSCode and Alacritty enable truecolor/hyperlinks without images; JetBrains-JediTerm and otherwise win32 enable only truecolor. Unknown terminals expose COLORTERM hint only. CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID alone does not suppress Ghostty.
entries.interfaces: TerminalCapabilities {images:'kitty'|'iterm2'|null,trueColor,hyperlinks}; CellDimensions {widthPx,heightPx}; detect/get/set/resetCapabilitiesCache and get/setCellDimensions. Environment: TERM,TERM_PROGRAM,TERMINAL_EMULATOR,COLORTERM,TMUX,KITTY_WINDOW_ID,GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR,WEZTERM_PANE,ITERM_SESSION_ID,WT_SESSION,WARP_SESSION_ID,WARP_TERMINAL_SESSION_UUID.

No corresponding tmux hyperlink probe or full color/hyperlink matrix exists in this module. Native cell setter also accepts0. Preserve native terminal-size fields and native capability overrides while separating cache reset semantics.

Share the agreed cell-size source with terminal reports and invalidate dependent renderers when it changes. Source audit did not execute the tmux probe or read user state.
