entries.title: Kitty and iTerm2 image serialization and deletion
entries.what: Transmit image payloads with correct continuation, cursor, placement and data-release controls, and support iTerm2 inline options.
entries.mechanism: isImageLine recognizes Kitty APC and iTerm2 File OSC anywhere in a line regardless of detected support, including large prefixed payloads. Kitty accepts already-base64 data, serializes a=T,f=100,q=2, adds C=1 only when moveCursor=false, and independently adds truthy columns,rows,imageId. Payloads up to4096 characters use one frame; longer payloads use4096-character chunks, full controls+m=1 on first, m=1 on intermediates and m=0 on last. Empty payload still produces a frame. Delete one uses a=d,d=I,i=id,q=2, all image data d=A,q=2, placements only d=a,q=2. iTerm2 defaults inline=1, emits defined width/height even0, base64-encodes optional name, emits preserveAspectRatio=0 only when false and terminates with BEL. renderImage always uses Kitty f=100 and does not itself transcode other image formats.
entries.interfaces: encodeKitty(base64,{columns,rows,imageId,moveCursor}); encodeITerm2(base64,{width,height,name,preserveAspectRatio,inline}); deletion strings; isImageLine; renderImage returning null when unsupported and otherwise sequence,columns,rows,imageId.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal_image.rs:178-281 encodes raw bytes to base64 and always sets C=1. It emits dimensions only when both are Some and supports native z-index. Crucial source-read defect: chunks are4000 characters; _m is computed but never inserted, so multi-chunk output has no m=1/m=0, and after the first frame controls are empty. Empty input returns no frame. This is reachable through rust:crates/ice-tui/src/image.rs:245-269 -> terminal_image.rs:429-445, not merely an unused helper. Native iTerm2 omits inline=1 and aspect option, uses unencoded name=idN, and may serialize empty semicolon fields. Native single-image deletion uses lowercase d=i (placement deletion, keeping image data) and omits q=2; all-data deletion uses d=A. The small native inline test at500-520 does not cover continuations or iTerm2. No runtime/protocol experiment was performed.
entries.port: Fix continuation construction at the encoder before higher-level cache work; preserve native z-index/raw-byte convenience through adapters. Model independent width/height,cursor and iTerm2 controls explicitly. Add quiet placement-only versus data-release operations and retain image-sequence detection independent of runtime capabilities. Verify boundary, empty, multi-frame and quiet-delete serialization in future implementation tests.
entries.priority_reason: The active native image component can emit malformed multi-chunk Kitty transmissions; higher-level image parity depends on repairing the wire output.

entries.title: Kitty metadata generations, placement reuse and vertical cropping
entries.what: Track transmitted image geometry and derive placement-only or cropped commands without retransmitting or corrupting the original line.
entries.mechanism: A global insertion-ordered map stores imageId,columns,rows,pixel width/height with an increasing transmissionGeneration. Registration replaces/reinserts an existing ID and evicts oldest entries above1000. renderImage registers only when the caller supplied imageId; ID allocation is separate. Metadata lookup parses the first Kitty header's decimal i. Placement parsing follows adjacent Kitty chunks while m=1, rejecting missing terminator,header or separator; it retains only i,p,x,y,w,h,X,Y,c,r,C,U,z,P,Q,H,V controls, prepends a=p,q=2, and returns imageId,generation,transmissionBytes,estimatedDecodedBytes=pixelWidth*pixelHeight*4,sequence and original-line replacement preserving prefix/suffix. Cropping requires known metadata, hiddenRows within[0,rows),positive visibleRows; clamp visible rows to remaining, retain unchanged full placement, compute source y=floor(pixelHeight*hidden/rows) and h from ceil bottom boundary with minimum1/clamping, then replace y,h,r in first header while preserving payload and all other line content.
entries.interfaces: register/getKittyImageMetadata; getKittyImagePlacement; cropKittyImageLine; KittyImageMetadata and KittyImagePlacement generation/byte-accounting contracts. Consumers include retained main/alternate-screen image caches.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal_image.rs:249-281 only scans changed old rows for a=T and decimal i before issuing placement deletion. There is no per-image geometry/generation map, complete transmission-span parser, a=p replacement or source-pixel crop contract in the fully read559-line module. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tui_alt_screen.rs:1-1471 retains image lines and deletes removed placements but lacks the corresponding bounded upload-reuse metadata. Existing row-based cleanup is partial infrastructure, not equivalent placement caching.
entries.port: Introduce an owned bounded metadata service and lossless Kitty transmission parser. Use generations plus byte estimates for renderer caching, preserve surrounding line text and carry crop controls into placement-only output. Scope cache lifetimes to terminal state and explicitly distinguish data eviction from visible placement deletion.
entries.priority_reason: Scrolled or partially visible images need reusable placement and pixel cropping without repeated large transmissions.

entries.title: Image dimensions and aspect-preserving cell fitting
entries.what: Read image geometry and fit it to explicit width/height cell limits using current pixel cell dimensions.
entries.mechanism: Size fitting floors and clamps maxWidthCells and optional maxHeightCells to at least1, clamps image pixel dimensions to1, computes min(widthScale,heightScale), allows upscaling, and ceil/clamps resulting columns and rows. Default cells are9x18; explicit zero cell dimensions are not validated. calculateImageRows shares fitting. Header helpers decode base64 and return null on caught failures. PNG requires24bytes and only first4 signature bytes before big-endian width/height at16/20. JPEG scans SOI and markers, recognizes SOF C0-C2, skips non-FF bytes and otherwise advances by2+segmentLength when length>=2. GIF checks87a/89a and reads little-endian width/height. WebP requires30bytes and RIFF/WEBP; handles VP8, VP8L dimension bits at21..24 and VP8X 24-bit fields at24/27. The public dispatcher uses exact MIME strings image/png,jpeg,gif,webp. These are header readers, not full decoders or validity checks.
entries.interfaces: ImageDimensions {widthPx,heightPx}; calculateImageRows; renderImage size result; getPng/Jpeg/Gif/Webp/ImageDimensions(base64,mimeType).
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal_image.rs:289-425 sniffs raw bytes independent of MIME, validates the full8-byte PNG signature and recognizes additional JPEG SOF forms; preserve those native strengths. Its WebP VP8L reads bytes17..20 instead of21..24 and has no VP8X case, so valid lossless headers can produce incorrect dimensions. calculate_image_rows computes integer(height+cellHeight-1)/cellHeight then narrows to u16, with no width-based fit and division by zero if the public cellHeight argument is0. The native Image component performs its own separate heuristic fit in image.rs:192-235, including a non-upscaling natural-width cap and floored width reduction, rather than the shared TS ceil/min-scale result.
entries.port: Unify dimension types and fitting behind a shared checked helper used by both component and direct rendering, while preserving stronger native signature/extra-JPEG handling. Correct WebP offsets/add VP8X and explicitly handle invalid cells and overflow. Provide a MIME-aware compatibility adapter without weakening native format sniffing.
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect header geometry or differing fit arithmetic breaks layout, cropping and reserved image rows.

entries.title: Image component, row reservation and informative fallback
entries.what: Render image attachments with stable IDs, bounded geometry and a readable, optionally clickable fallback.
entries.mechanism: Constructor stores base64,MIME,theme,options and explicit dimensions or header result, falling back to800x600. It accepts a reusable imageId; otherwise allocates an ID lazily only for Kitty. Actual random formula produces1..0xfffffffe (despite a wider comment). Render caches only by width until invalidate, including capabilities/cell-dependent output. Max width is max(1,min(width-2,optionMaxWidth or60)); default max height is ceil(maxWidth*cellWidth/cellHeight), a square pixel box. Call renderImage with moveCursor=false and explicit max bounds. Kitty returns the sequence on first row followed by rows-1 empties; iTerm2 puts empties first and then cursor-up(rows-1)+sequence last. Fallback is one themed, width-truncated line, formatted [Image: optionalFilename [optionalMime] optionalWxH]. Absolute home paths are shortened only at home boundary; absolute filenames become file:// OSC8 links only when hyperlink capability is true. Relative/basename paths remain plain.

entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/image.rs:36-379 reserves corresponding image rows and iTerm cursor-up ordering; preserve this existing parity. Expose stable caller IDs and explicit geometry, compose MIME/path fallback through shared OSC8/truncation utilities, and document rather than imply URL retrieval.
entries.priority_reason: Users need correct attachment sizing and useful fallback information on terminals without image support.

entries.title: Loader animation, configurable frames and render scheduling
entries.what: Animate an optional indicator independently of rendering, with deterministic start/stop and live message/indicator updates.
entries.mechanism: Loader extends Text with horizontal padding1,vertical0 and prepends one blank line. Construction immediately setIndicator/start; default ten Braille frames rotate every80ms. Explicit indicator object makes frames verbatim (including default frames when omitted), otherwise spinnerColor is applied. Frames are copied; empty hides spinner and its separator, singleton stays static, >1 creates an interval. intervalMs is accepted when truthy and>0, otherwise80. setIndicator resets index0 and restarts; start updates text/render request then replaces timer; stop clears timer but retains displayed state. Each tick advances modulo frame count and updates display/requestRender; setMessage also updates immediately. The interval is not unref'ed in this source.

entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/loader.rs:24-191 has Vec<char> options (no multichar/ANSI frames), frame_duration_ms and matching80ms constant, but render always calls advance regardless of running and no timer consults frame_duration_ms. start changes running/start_time, stop only running. Empty spinner_chars reaches modulo zero in advance, including render; current_char's fallback does not prevent it. Preserve elapsed/progress variants as opt-in native features. Expose a live indicator setter for appearance consumers and ensure disposal stops timers.
entries.priority_reason: Render-frequency-dependent animation and empty-frame panics prevent compatible live appearance customization.

entries.title: Cancellable loader signal and configured cancel input
entries.what: Give asynchronous loader users an abort signal and callback tied to the configured selection-cancel action.
entries.mechanism: Each CancellableLoader owns one AbortController for its lifetime. handleInput checks current global keybindings for tui.select.cancel; on every match it calls abort() and then onAbort if present. AbortSignal is monotonic/idempotent but onAbort can fire again for repeated matching input. Cancellation itself does not stop Loader animation; dispose stops it. No automatic reset controller is provided.
entries.interfaces: signal,aborted,onAbort?,handleInput(data),dispose; inherited Loader operations; tui.select.cancel binding.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/loader.rs:193-281 offers a callback and explicit cancel() that stops the loader, but no abort-token/signal or aborted state, no input handling override, and a hard-coded 'Press Ctrl+C to cancel' hint only while running. The callback is invoked while holding its mutex, so a callback that re-registers itself through on_cancel would re-enter the same lock. Existing native ProgressLoader at283-377 is a separate extra, not a replacement for this signal contract.
entries.port: Add reusable cancellation-token state and route configured cancel input through the actual focus/input owner. Release callback locks before invocation, keep stop/dispose lifecycle explicit, and generate any optional native hint from active bindings. Preserve native direct cancel convenience with documented semantics.
entries.priority_reason: Extensions and dialogs need a reliable async cancellation contract rather than a display-only hint.

entries.title: Transient alternate-screen flash messages
entries.what: Compose multiple independently expiring transient notifications in the alternate-screen frame.
entries.mechanism: flash(message,duration=1000) assigns an increasing ID, schedules a timeout at max(0,duration), unrefs it, appends the entry and requests render. Expiry finds that ID, removes only it and requests render; multiple flashes retain insertion order and independent lifetimes. render maps each to a leading/trailing-space padded message truncated without ellipsis to width, then SGR7 reverse and SGR27 reset. dispose clears every timer and list without requesting another render. invalidate is empty. TuiAltScreen composes this layer after selection/action-link hover and clears it at lifecycle transitions.
entries.interfaces: AltScreenFlashContainer(requestRender),flash(message,durationMs?),render,invalidate,dispose; TuiAltScreen.flash.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tui_alt_screen.rs:1-1471 has no equivalent transient flash queue/layer/timer. A bounded full-directory symbol search in crates/ice-tui/src returned no Flash/flash implementation; this is absence in primitive scope, not a claim about application-level status messages elsewhere.
entries.port: Add a transient layer with independent cancellation handles and explicit lifecycle ownership, using the renderer's scheduling callback. Keep the layer outside document layout, preserve insertion order, and dispose without leaving timers or prior-screen artifacts.
entries.priority_reason: Copy feedback and short fullscreen status messages need bounded lifetimes without mutating transcript content.

entries.title: Unicode word navigation and atomic segments
entries.what: Move and delete by linguistic word, punctuation run or caller-defined atomic marker without merging distinct boundaries.
entries.mechanism: Backward slices text before the UTF16 cursor, segments with Intl.Segmenter or a supplied segment callback, skips trailing whitespace unless atomic, then consumes exactly one atomic segment, one word-like segment up to its last ASCII punctuation boundary, or a contiguous nonword/nonwhitespace run. Forward symmetrically skips leading whitespace then consumes one unit; inside word-like segments it stops at the first ASCII punctuation. Atomic checks precede whitespace/word logic. Word segmentation therefore splits CJK linguistic units and handles a whole paste marker independent of spaces inside it. Examples from read tests: forward hello world at0=>5 and at5=>11; foo.bar visits0,3,4,7; backward7=>4=>3=>0.
entries.interfaces: findWordBackward/Forward(text,cursor,options?); WordNavigationOptions.segment(text),isAtomicSegment(segment); UTF16 source positions require an explicit native position adapter.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/word_navigation.rs:5-201 uses Unicode scalar indices and a fixed ASCII boundary list. Forward skips the current word plus subsequent punctuation/space, giving hello world0=>6, and backward skips punctuation together with whitespace before a word. It has no linguistic segmentation or atomic marker hooks. Non-ASCII punctuation absent from the boundary list is treated as a word character; a cursor beyond scalar length can index out of bounds in backward helpers. Keep native line/current-word/word-end helpers, but do not treat them as source-equivalent word movement.
entries.port: Create a shared segment/position abstraction that preserves grapheme-safe storage while exposing linguistic word and atomic-marker boundaries. Keep punctuation runs separate, adopt the exact direction order, and bind both Input and Editor navigation/deletion to it. Clamp public out-of-range positions without weakening existing native byte-safety.
entries.priority_reason: Word deletion is user-visible destructive editing; punctuation, CJK and paste markers need precise shared boundaries.

entries.title: Kill-ring and undo snapshot semantics
entries.what: Retain deleted-text history and detached undo snapshots with the source's accumulation, rotation and capacity behavior.
entries.mechanism: KillRing ignores empty text; every nonaccumulating push adds an entry even if equal to the latest. Accumulation replaces latest with prepend(text+latest) for backward deletion or append(latest+text) for forward. peek reads latest, rotate moves latest to oldest when length>1 and permanently changes subsequent yank order. There is no source capacity limit or deduplication. UndoStack.push structuredClone's arbitrary state, pop returns the detached snapshot directly, clear empties and length counts; no limit,redo or action grouping exists in the utility itself (consumers own grouping).
entries.interfaces: KillRing.push(text,{prepend,accumulate?}),peek,rotate,length; UndoStack<S>.push/pop/clear/length.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/kill_ring.rs:10-134 matches accumulation and equivalent rotation using newest at front, but defaults to64entries and deduplicates identical successive nonaccumulating text. It offers useful custom capacity, reverse rotation,clear/inspection extras. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/undo_stack.rs:7-236 defaults to256states and takes owned T without cloning (despite a Clone bound); detachment depends on caller's T and cloning policy. Actual native Input snapshots clone String and Editor state must be assessed separately; a generic owned Arc is not a deep clone. Preserve native RedoStack/UndoRedoManager and optional limits without silently claiming unbounded/deep-clone compatibility.
entries.port: Expose explicit compatibility capacity/dedup policy and document snapshot ownership for native state. Preserve redo/limits as native options, ensure undo snapshots own all mutable editor/paste metadata, and let consumer action state determine accumulation/coalescing.
entries.priority_reason: Different history retention and duplicate suppression change yank-pop and undo results after otherwise identical edits.

entries.title: Fuzzy score precision, token matching and alphanumeric fallback
entries.what: Produce the same matching set and stable ordering for commands, providers and other selector text.
entries.mechanism: Case-fold both strings; empty query matches score0 and longer query fails. Greedy in-order UTF16 matches score lower-is-better: consecutive counter starts from lastIndex=-1 so a match at text index0 already receives -5; successive consecutive matches subtract counter*5, gaps after a prior match add2 per skipped unit; boundaries at start or whitespace,-,_ ,.,/,colon subtract10; every match adds index*0.1; exact normalized equality subtracts100. Only after primary failure, anchored ASCII all-letters+all-digits or reversed two-block query is swapped, and a successful swapped score gets+5. fuzzyFilter splits trimmed query on whitespace/slash, requires every token independently against the same text, sums scores and stable-sorts; empty/tokenless query returns the original array.
entries.interfaces: FuzzyMatch {matches,score:number}; fuzzyMatch and generic fuzzyFilter(items,query,getText).
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/fuzzy.rs:35-267 mostly ports matching/filtering and keeps a stable score sort, but score is i32 and each0.1*position penalty is individually truncated; consecutive bonus excludes the first index0 match. Matching positions are Unicode scalars rather than UTF16. swap_alphanumeric does not validate both entire blocks: it can skip intervening punctuation and accepts trailing mixed characters, producing matches the source's anchored regex rejects. Keep borrowed/owned native filter variants and Unicode-safe traversal, but calibrate scoring/matching contract explicitly.
entries.port: Use exact scaled integer tenths or floating score, reproduce first-match and stable-tie rules, and restrict swap fallback to the two anchored ASCII forms. Define non-BMP indexing intentionally in the compatibility layer and keep native owned/borrowed APIs.
entries.priority_reason: Subtle score and fallback differences reorder suggestions across many dialogs and can introduce false matches.

entries.title: Single-line input mutation, paste and undo integration
entries.what: Provide source-compatible single-line editing, configured actions, bracketed paste and repeatable kill/yank/undo behavior.
entries.mechanism: setValue preserves/clamps existing cursor; a separate setValueAndMoveCursorToEnd places it at end; neither resets history/action state. Input first buffers bracketed paste across chunks, strips one start marker wherever found, finds end across accumulated data, inserts content atomically then recursively handles trailing input. Paste removes CRLF/CR/LF and expands tabs to four spaces; it does not apply the ordinary-input C0/DEL/C1 rejection to other pasted controls. Configured cancel,undo,submit (plus literal LF),deletion,kill/yank and movement precede Kitty printable decoding and ordinary input. Left/right/backspace/delete consume Intl graphemes. Word and line kills snapshot each change and accumulate by prior kill action/direction. Yank snapshots and inserts newest; yank-pop only after yank with>1entries replaces the immediately preceding yanked span and permanently rotates ring. Undo restores only value/cursor and clears lastAction, leaving ring intact. Typing coalesces after a type-word action except each whitespace input pushes a new snapshot, so a space and following word form one unit. Boundary no-op kills do not reset prior action; cursor operations generally do. Submit/cancel callbacks do not clear input.
entries.interfaces: Input.getValue,setValue,setValueAndMoveCursorToEnd,onSubmit,onEscape,focused,handleInput; action IDs tui.select.cancel,tui.editor.undo/delete*/cursor*/yank/yankPop,tui.input.submit; InputState {value,cursor}.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/input.rs:17-589 already maps scalar positions to byte boundaries before splicing, safely snapshots outside the state lock and notifies after unlocking; preserve these fixes, including native tests767-889. set_value always moves to end, so cursor-preserving setter is missing. Movement/deletion operates on scalars, splitting combining/ZWJ graphemes. handle_key hard-codes Crossterm mappings; the stored Keybindings is unused, Ctrl+_ orCtrl+/ undo differs from source binding, Alt+Y never reaches private yank_pop, and Component has no input override. External host handle_key/handle_paste remains the actual native route. Paste cleanup matches, but empty paste/empty insertion skips snapshot. No raw bracketed-paste buffer or Kitty decode adapter exists here; native event parsing can supply typed paste instead. Native on_change/masking/custom prompt are extras. Callback invocations retain their respective callback mutex, so re-registering the same callback slot from inside it is non-reentrant even though state-lock deadlocks have been fixed.
entries.port: Bind editing actions through the shared key registry at the actual native event owner and expose typed-paste delivery. Add cursor-preserving setter, grapheme movement/deletion and yank-pop route; retain byte-safe splicing and lock-release order. Keep native on_change/masking and release callback locks before invocation. Match source state/history transitions rather than clearing history implicitly.
entries.priority_reason: Input dialogs currently differ in cursor placement, key customization, Unicode deletion and yank-pop despite substantial native editing support.

entries.title: Single-line input horizontal window and focus cursor rendering
entries.what: Keep the caret visible within a horizontally scrolled, grapheme-safe single-line input.
entries.mechanism: The fixed prompt is '> ' and availableWidth=width-2; nonpositive width still returns that prompt. If text visual width<available width it fits with a cursor cell, otherwise reserve one extra column only when cursor is at text end, center the window near the caret except near either edge, and use strict column slicing. Derive the visible UTF16 caret from the sliced prefix, invert the entire next grapheme or one blank cell even when unfocused, and emit zero-width hardware marker immediately before it only when focused. Right-pad to available visual width; no render cache.
entries.interfaces: Input.render(width),focused; CURSOR_MARKER; shared visibleWidth/sliceByColumn/grapheme segmentation.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/input.rs:598-711 follows the same general window positioning and has a corrected caret marker after the prefix, with regression tests803-850. It displays one scalar at cursor, inverts only while focused, appends SGR0 and omits source right-padding. Native strict slicing inherits TUI-203 differences. Custom prompt width is measured visually; masked bullets and an unfocused placeholder are useful native additions, though placeholder text is not width-clipped in this path. Keep those extras and corrected marker logic.
entries.port: Share grapheme-aware window/caret layout and source padding/focus compatibility, preserve native custom prompt,masking and placeholder options, and clip placeholder output. Keep marker position derived from visible prefix rather than byte/scalar index.
entries.priority_reason: Caret and Unicode clipping consistency is necessary for usable IME and narrow dialog inputs.

entries.title: Asynchronous autocomplete provider and slash-command contracts
entries.what: Allow cancellable asynchronous suggestions over a multiline cursor, command metadata and command-specific argument completion.
entries.mechanism: Provider receives lines,cursorLine,cursorCol plus mandatory AbortSignal and optional force, returns a Promise of {items,prefix} or null, exposes optional triggerCharacters/shouldTriggerFileCompletion and owns applyCompletion. Combined provider captures commands,basePath and optional fd path. @ token detection always takes priority, even force. Otherwise a nonforced line starting exactly '/' uses command logic: before first ASCII space fuzzy-match names (SlashCommand.name or AutocompleteItem.value), display argumentHint followed by ' — '+description when both exist; after space find exact command name and await its argument-completion callback with all remaining argument text. Missing callback/nonarray/empty result returns null without falling back to files; callback errors propagate. Forced calls bypass slash command routing. shouldTriggerFileCompletion returns false if trimmed prefix begins '/' and contains no ASCII space, including slash paths; otherwise true. Signal cancellation is used in fd path, not automatically checked around command callbacks/direct listings.
entries.interfaces: AutocompleteProvider,AutocompleteSuggestions,AutocompleteItem {value,label,description?},SlashCommand {name,description?,argumentHint?,getArgumentCompletions?}; positions are UTF16 within current line.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/autocomplete.rs:36-122 exposes a synchronous whole-input trait returning byte start/end,is_path and native item flags. No AbortSignal/async/trigger characters/force/applyCompletion or argument callback/hint exists. Slash provider at262-354 stores names including slash, fuzzy-matches the entire prefix after '/', has no argument routing and sets insert_space=false. Combined391-404 chooses first successful provider; defaults install slash before filepath rather than @ precedence. Its dynamically discovered command append and manager/provider extensibility are native capabilities to retain. Manager invokes provider while holding its provider mutex; replacing provider from inside callback would re-enter it.
entries.port: Introduce an async cancel-aware request/result contract with explicit line/position units and adapter for synchronous native providers. Add command hint/argument callbacks and exact routing/force semantics, retain discovered command composition, and clone provider handles before invoking callbacks. Editor stale-result ownership is a separate integration entry.
entries.priority_reason: Command arguments and asynchronous custom providers are missing at the native interface, blocking downstream editor parity.

entries.title: Direct filesystem completion, quoted tokens and display paths
entries.what: Complete local paths with exact token boundaries, home/relative preservation, symlink handling and quoted directory continuation.
entries.mechanism: Token delimiters are space,tab,double/single quote,equals. Double-quote scanning toggles on every quote without escape interpretation; an unclosed quote beginning at a token boundary, optionally immediately after boundary '@', yields the whole quoted prefix. Otherwise use the last delimiter. Natural path suggestions require slash,leading dot,~/ or empty token after literal space; forced extraction accepts any token including empty. Parse @ and opening quote separately. Expand only ~/ or exact~, preserving trailing slash; resolve relative directory against captured basePath. Empty,./,../,~,~/,/ roots and trailing slash list that directory; otherwise split parent/basename. Read entries synchronously, case-insensitive prefix filter, stat symlinks to identify directories (broken/inaccessible link treated as file), preserve ./,~/,absolute/relative display forms and normalize backslashes to '/'. Append '/' to directory paths, quote if already quoted or containing a space, and show basename label. Sort by value.endsWith('/') then label.localeCompare: quoted directory values end in a quote, so they do not receive that directory-first branch. Catch directory failures to[].
entries.interfaces: CombinedAutocompleteProvider basePath constructor, quoted/@ prefix extraction, getFileSuggestions; paths read by readdirSync/searchDir and statSync/fullPath. These source filesystem operations were not executed during audit.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/autocomplete.rs:124-260 has a basic file provider. snap_cursor prevents invalid UTF8 slicing but accepts ambiguous caller units by snapping rather than converting. Token scan treats a quote as delimiter, so the later token.starts_with('"') branch cannot preserve a quoted path containing spaces. @ is removed from replacement start; bare@ then has empty prefix and fails the emptiness guard. Paths containing separators ignore root_path, use native Path parent/file_name even for trailing slash, and have no home expansion/display-prefix preservation; returned text is only entry basename. It caps directory iteration at50 before filtering, has no sort, does not follow symlink directory metadata and unconditionally calls as_directory() for every result, including files (insert_space still reflects actual is_dir). No force/natural-trigger distinction exists. Preserve configurable root/max results and byte-safety while repairing semantics.
entries.port: Build one parser/resolver retaining source span,quote/@ state and display base, then perform bounded native listings with correct directory flags and post-filter ordering/limits. Preserve symlink and home/relative handling. Keep source's quoted-directory sort quirk explicit if exact parity is required rather than claiming idealized directory-first behavior.
entries.priority_reason: Quoted,home,nested and symlink paths currently produce different or incomplete replacements in the native provider.

entries.title: Recursive @ attachment search, ranking and cancellation
entries.what: Search recursively for @ attachment paths with cancellation, scoped directories and stable ranked results.
entries.mechanism:
Absent fdPath or pre-aborted signal returns[]. Normalize query separators; if text before final slash resolves to an existing directory (~/,absolute or basePath-relative), scope fd there and search only trailing query, preserving the display base. Otherwise search entire basePath with original query. fd argv: --base-directory dir --max-results100 --type f --type d --follow --hidden and three .git exclusions; add --full-path when query includes slash. A slash-bearing query is converted to escaped path segments separated by a regex matching either separator, preserving trailing separator; a no-slash query is passed as-is, so it retains fd regex interpretation. Spawn with stdin ignored and stdout/stderr pipes, accumulate stdout, settle once on error/close; nonzero,empty or aborted returns[]. Abort SIGKILLs child if exitCode null, then settlement waits for close/error; listener removed on finish. stderr is piped but not consumed, and no explicit timeout/output cap beyond fd max-results is implemented.

Parse newline output, normalize backslashes and infer directory from trailing slash; exclude .git paths again. Score nonempty query against basename exact100,prefix80,substring50,or full-path substring30, +10 directories only if score>0; empty query score1. Drop zero scores, stable descending sort, keep top20. Build @ values with quoting and directory suffix, basename labels and full display path description. Check abort again after fd completion. Tests use temporary fixtures and conditionally skip when fd absent; all were source-read only.
entries.interfaces: CombinedAutocompleteProvider fdPath; AbortSignal; recursive query/baseDir/displayBase; process/error/abort contract; attachment AutocompleteItem metadata.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/autocomplete.rs:124-260 only lists one directory synchronously. The fully read483-line module has no recursive fd/native walk,ignore-file/symlink search,scoped@ ranking,20result selection,cancellation or process-lifecycle interface. This is missing within primitive autocomplete scope; ordinary filepath completion is existing partial infrastructure, not equivalent recursion.
entries.port: Implement a cancellable native recursive search or fd adapter preserving ignore/hidden/follow and ranking semantics; make base/display paths explicit and handle child completion once. Improve bounded output/stderr draining as an intentional native robustness measure. Do not introduce a new external executable requirement if an in-process walker can satisfy the exact behavior.
entries.priority_reason: Recursive attachment discovery is a primary autocomplete mode and is absent from the native provider.

entries.title: Autocomplete application and quoted directory caret placement
entries.what: Apply the chosen suggestion to precisely the requested prefix while preserving suffix text and usable quote/directory caret position.
entries.mechanism: Clone lines, retain same cursorLine, replace current prefix-length span before cursor and keep suffix. If source prefix is quoted, item ends in quote and suffix begins quote, drop exactly one duplicate closing quote. Slash command classification is prefix starts'/',beforePrefix.trim empty and no further slash: insert '/' + item.value + one space and place caret after it, retaining suffix. @ attachment adds a space only for nondirectory label (directory determined by label.endsWith('/')); for a quoted directory place caret before closing quote. Generic command-argument heuristic (text before cursor contains slash and space) and generic path branch both insert item.value without extra space, using the same quoted-directory caret offset. This is syntactic classification, not verified against the command registry; a top-level one-segment absolute-path prefix can enter the slash-name branch.
entries.interfaces: AutocompleteProvider.applyCompletion(lines,cursorLine,cursorCol,item,prefix) -> new lines/cursor; values,labels and quote/space policy.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/autocomplete.rs:93-113 returns byte start/end and is_path without a provider applyCompletion hook. The actual native consumer is rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/autocomplete.rs:119-162, not Editor itself: it re-queries suggestions, clamps chosen index and span endpoints to text length, preserves text before/after the span and restores multiline byte cursor using helpers21-51. It assumes provider ranges are valid UTF8 boundaries and ordered; custom malformed ranges can still panic despite length clamps. For insert_space it appends the space after the entire preserved suffix, while cursor calculation assumes it belongs immediately after completion. The append condition tests the entire replaced document for trailing slash, but caret uses top.text.ends_with('/'), so these can disagree. set_text clears all folded-paste payloads and takes no undo snapshot, another loss of transaction semantics. Native menu/navigation at54-114/170-201 is an existing host capability to retain.
entries.port: Add a provider-owned application hook or an equivalent explicit replacement plan including suffix adjustment and caret position. Keep native item flags but adapt label/value semantics consistently, and ensure byte/character conversion is explicit at the editor boundary. In the actual CLI acceptance path, insert any completion space before the preserved suffix, validate/snap provider spans, and apply the replacement as one editor transaction that preserves unrelated paste payloads and can be undone.
entries.priority_reason: Suggestions are only usable when insertion preserves suffix text and leaves the caret inside quoted directories for continued completion.

entries.title: Editor state access and atomic programmatic replacement
entries.what: Expose raw and expanded multiline text, defensively copied lines/cursor and predictable replacement/insertion operations without confusing text offsets with terminal cells.
entries.mechanism: State contains at least one logical line and UTF16 cursorLine/cursorCol. getText joins LF; getLines copies; getExpandedText iterates paste registry in insertion order, replacing each registered marker with a function-returned literal body so dollar replacement syntax is inert. This can expand a later-ID marker introduced inside an earlier paste body; it is not a single nonrecursive pass. setText cancels completion, exits history, clears last action, normalizes CRLF/CR to LF and tabs to four spaces; when text differs it captures the full pre-change snapshot. It always clears paste registry/counter, positions at the end and calls onChange even for the same text. insertTextAtCursor ignores empty input, cancels completion/history and captures one snapshot before normalization/splicing; preserves both existing prefix and suffix and places cursor after inserted content, with one change callback. pasteText routes to paste preprocessing, not plain insertion.
entries.interfaces: Editor.getText/getExpandedText/getLines/getCursor/setText/insertTextAtCursor/pasteText; EditorState and source UTF16 offsets; EditorComponent abstraction. The custom EditorComponent interface requires getText/setText/handleInput plus the Component render/invalidate contract. onSubmit/onChange properties are optional despite the comment heading; history, insertion, paste, expanded text, autocomplete provider, borderColor, padding and dropdown-height setters are optional. The interface documents expanded-text fallback to getText; caller integration belongs to extension/application entries.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:269-450 exposes equivalent raw/expanded text and byte cursor access, but set_text splits LF without CR/tab normalization, moves to row0/col0, clears pastes, does not capture undo or exit history and leaves any selection anchor intact. expand_pastes is one regex replacement pass. insert at795-857 normalizes line endings but not tabs and coalesces with prior inserts; selection replacement is a native extra. snap_boundary at146-165 and set_cursor at554-562 protect ordinary byte-position setters; preserve them. Native selection, redo and optional placeholder/initial text should remain available alongside source-compatible operations.
entries.port: Define byte-versus-source offset adapters and explicit atomic replace/insert APIs. Restore source normalization, end-caret, snapshot and callback order, reset stale selection appropriately, and keep native selection/redo capabilities. Document recursive marker expansion as source behavior and choose a bounded safe expansion policy explicitly rather than accidentally changing literal paste content.
entries.priority_reason: External editor, clipboard, completion and extension operations need predictable replacement and undo semantics.

entries.title: Editor paste framing, sanitization and large-paste folding
entries.what: Treat a bracketed or programmatic paste as one editing action, retain multiline content, and fold large input into a display marker without silently changing expanded data.
entries.mechanism: The editor buffers bracketed-paste chunks until ESC[201~, handles trailing input recursively and routes completed text through handlePaste. Paste cancels completion/history, resets last action and captures an undo snapshot before cleanup. Decode CSI-u Ctrl-letter sequences into control bytes, normalize CRLF/CR and tabs to four spaces, then remove code units below32 except LF; DEL and C1 remain. If cleaned text begins /,~ or . and the preceding character is ASCII word, prepend one space. Fold when line count>10 or UTF16 length>1000, allocating increasing ID and marker '[paste #N +L lines]' for multiline or '[paste #N C chars]' otherwise; store cleaned body. Insert directly without natural completion triggers. Even all-filtered input has already captured a snapshot but emits no change callback.
entries.interfaces: Bracketed paste delimiters; pasteText(text); getText folded form vs getExpandedText expanded form; snapshot includes paste map/counter.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:452-506 has CSI-u/CR/tab cleanup and large-paste registry, preserving the basic feature. It counts Unicode scalars rather than UTF16 units, omits path-prefix separation and returns before snapshot for empty cleaned content. Both small and large pastes call insert-style undo grouping, so adjacent typing/pastes can share a snapshot. Raw handle_input at1570-1574 is a stub; the native host delivers Paste events directly, which is a valid architecture to preserve while matching the editing transaction. Inline paste tests at2227-2420 verify basic folding/cleanup but not UTF16 threshold, independent adjacent paste undo or path separator policy.
entries.port: Keep structured native Paste events and add an atomic paste transaction with precise cleanup, source-equivalent thresholds and path boundary behavior. Make delimiter handling a raw-input adapter responsibility when supporting EditorComponent.handleInput. Preserve expanded literal bytes and add source-derived threshold/undo cases without invoking external clipboard or a real terminal during this audit.
entries.priority_reason: Large pasted prompts and file paths must remain recoverable and independently undoable.

entries.title: Paste-marker ownership, deletion and collision-free registry renumbering
entries.what: Keep marker display text, atomic cursor behavior, payload ownership and undo restoration consistent after deletion and renumbering.
entries.mechanism: Only regex-shaped markers whose ID exists in the paste registry are atomic. Grapheme and word segmenters merge valid marker spans; unknown manually typed markers remain ordinary text. Backspace after a valid marker captures text+registry+counter, removes its registry entry, decrements counter, moves higher IDs in sorted ascending order and rewrites higher marker IDs throughout all logical lines. Forward delete removes a whole atomic marker but does not remove/renumber its registry entry; word/line kills likewise retain registry entries. Undo restores all three structures. Preserve these distinctions as actual source behavior. Source caveats: backspace rewrites text before cutting with pre-rewrite offsets, so digit-width changes in earlier markers can invalidate its slice position; rewriting a valid bare marker with no suffix interpolates undefined for that suffix. A port should perform the deletion and a collision-free rewrite from one stable snapshot rather than copying those defects.
entries.interfaces: Registered marker regex '[paste #ID( +L lines| C chars)?]'; validPasteIds; deep EditorSnapshot; getExpandedText literal replacement.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:167-193 recognizes marker syntax without consulting registry for left/right/backspace; manually typed marker-like text is incorrectly atomic. delete_forward at909-936 removes one scalar instead of a whole marker. remove_paste at415-450 collects higher HashMap keys without sorting, then removes old ID and inserts old-1. Reachable backspace at859-903 deletes a registered marker and calls this: if higher IDs3 then2 are visited after deleting1, payload3 overwrites payload2 at key2, then the later removal moves payload3 again to1, losing payload2 and leaving rewritten marker2 unresolved. Order depends on HashMap iteration. Native deletion occurs before renumbering, which avoids the source's stale-slice defect and must be preserved. Native tests at2286-2320 cover only one higher entry2→1, not this collision.
