Rebuild a new registry from immutable entries or sort ascending before moving IDs; rewrite text and cursor from a stable deletion result. Retain complete snapshots and intentionally define forward-delete registry retention. Add deterministic three-or-more marker cases with out-of-order display and crossing9→10 IDs; repair the Rust data-loss defect before relying on marker expansion.
entries.priority_reason: A normal delete with several folded pastes can destroy stored prompt content in the current native implementation.

entries.title: Editor undo transaction boundaries and full snapshot restoration
entries.what: Restore text, cursor and folded paste content in user-sized actions while retaining native redo as an additional capability.
entries.mechanism: Undo snapshots deep-clone state, paste map and counter. Consecutive nonwhitespace typing shares a 'type-word' action; every whitespace insertion captures a new snapshot, then following word characters coalesce with it. Movement, history entry, newline, paste, programmatic insert/replacement, completion, kills and yanks create/reset action boundaries as their handlers specify; no-op deletion does not push. Entering history captures once before browsing. Undo exits history, restores snapshot, clears last action and preferred visual column and emits onChange. It does not explicitly cancel completion, reset scrollOffset or clear snappedFrom; record these as source limitations, not stronger guarantees. Submit clears undo. Kill-ring contents are not included in undo snapshots.
entries.interfaces: EditorSnapshot {state,pastes,pasteCounter}; UndoStack.createUndoStack cloning callback; undo key action and callback sequence.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:592-648 stores deep native text/paste snapshots and a200-entry undo cap plus redo stack. push_undo suppresses any consecutive 'insert', including spaces/pastes; cursor movement does not reliably clear last_action. set_text has no snapshot. backspace can push for a no-op. Ctrl-J at1237-1241 inserts without any undo snapshot; Shift-Enter uses ordinary insert coalescing. Native undo/redo correctly restores paste registry and clears selection, which must be preserved. Inline undo tests at1943-2053 explicitly expect 'hello'+' world' as one unit and do not establish source grouping.
entries.port: Centralize transaction types and action transitions instead of assigning last_action indirectly inside snapshot helpers. Match source word/whitespace/atomic operation boundaries, keep owned snapshot isolation and native redo, and invalidate stale completion appropriately when undo changes a request snapshot. Make any history/scroll reset strengthening explicit.
entries.priority_reason: Undo must not discard unrelated typing or lose folded paste bodies after programmatic edits.

entries.title: Editor history browsing with preserved draft and visual-boundary routing
entries.what: Browse recent submitted prompts while preserving the editable draft and allowing ordinary movement inside multiline history entries.
entries.mechanism: addToHistory trims, ignores empty/consecutive duplicates, prepends newest and caps100; submission itself does not append. Up enters history only at first visual row when empty/already browsing/cursor at protected prompt prefix; a nonempty first-row cursor farther right first moves to line start. On initial browse capture one undo snapshot and a deep draft state. Older entries position at start; newer entries position at end; moving beyond newest restores exact draft cursor, resets sticky/snap/scroll and calls onChange. Opposite direction inside a multiline history entry moves through its visual rows until a boundary. Mutating input and setText/undo exit browsing. History transitions do not record every visited entry as a new undo unit.
entries.interfaces: Editor.addToHistory(text); historyIndex/draft; protected getPromptPrefixLength; cursor up/down routing after autocomplete.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:258-267 stores history and history_index, but the full implementation has no equivalent browse/draft methods or Up/Down history route. submit at1182-1197 appends every nonempty untrimmed result without dedup/cap, then index=len. Native Up/Down at965-1001 always moves logical lines and cannot recover prior entries. Host history adapters may exist outside this primitive; do not infer that the entire application lacks history solely from these fields.
entries.port: Implement explicit history storage/browse state with a saved draft and integrate only at the appropriate first/last visual boundary after completion handling. Keep persistence/application history ownership outside the primitive and avoid double-appending when the caller supplies addToHistory.
entries.priority_reason: History is a normal prompt editing operation and must not overwrite the active draft or interfere with multiline cursor movement.

entries.title: Editor input precedence, newline workarounds and submit lifecycle
entries.what: Resolve input consistently across jump mode, paste, undo, completion, text editing and submission, using configurable actions and defined callback ordering.
entries.mechanism: Priority is disabled-completion cleanup, pending jump, bracketed paste, parent copy passthrough, undo, open completion menu, Tab completion, deletion/kill/yank/navigation and newline/submit, then printable decoding. Newline accepts configured keys plus raw LF, ESC+CR, Shift-Enter legacy encodings and compound input; raw LF is newline even when Enter submits. At submit, a backslash immediately before cursor is removed and converted to newline; when submit is configured to Shift-Enter, the special backslash+bareEnter path can submit instead. disableSubmit gates submission. submit expands then trims the whole prompt, cancels completion and resets text/pastes/counter/history cursor/scroll/undo before onChange('') and then onSubmit(text); it does not itself add history. Printable Kitty/modifyOtherKeys decoding is used before a permissive fallback whose first codepoint is>=32.
entries.interfaces: onChange,onSubmit,disableSubmit; getKeybindings dynamic action matches; Editor.handleInput raw sequences; newline/submit/copy/tab actions.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1158-1388 uses hardcoded Crossterm KeyCode/modifiers despite holding a keybindings manager. Raw handle_input1570-1574 always returnsfalse. Plain Enter/LF/CR submit, Shift-Enter inserts via normal undo grouping, Ctrl-J inserts without snapshot. There is no disableSubmit or backslash workaround. submit passes expanded but untrimmed text, appends internal history, invokes on_submit before clear/on_change and retains other editing state. Existing normalized host input is valid and should remain; add a binding-aware action layer instead of routing raw bytes through the host a second time. Native event-kind/release filtering is caller-owned, so this entry does not assert double typing in the actual CLI.
entries.port: Separate structured key decoding from action dispatch, consult configured actions in the native editor, and implement source precedence/newline/submit transaction order. Preserve native selection shortcuts and redo in nonconflicting contexts. Define callback reentrancy and ensure a submit callback cannot be silently overwritten by a subsequent clear.
entries.priority_reason: Enter and multiline paste behavior directly changes the prompt sent to the model; callback ordering affects host integrations.

entries.title: Editor grapheme edits and Unicode-safe word cursor operations
entries.what: Move, delete and kill complete graphemes or registered paste atoms without creating invalid offsets or panicking on ordinary Unicode input.
entries.mechanism: Left/right and backspace/forward delete use Intl grapheme segments merged with owned paste markers, cross logical newline boundaries and keep cursor at the segment start/end. Word operations delegate to the Unicode/ASCII-punctuation segment policy, treating valid markers as one nonpunctuation atom. Backward/forward word kills at line start/end delete the newline and merge lines; line kills do likewise at the boundary. Mutations exit history, reset sticky action state, emit onChange and refresh/cancel completion where source handlers specify. Protected prompt prefix clamps first-line cursor lower bound.
entries.interfaces: Editor moveCursor,deleteWordBackward/Forward,deleteToLineStart/End,backspace,deleteForward; UTF16 source indices and grapheme atom boundaries.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:859-1096 keeps ordinary character edits byte-safe but splits extended grapheme clusters by Unicode scalar and gives only backward-delete/horizontal marker support. More seriously, kill_word_backward at1052 passes byte cursor_col into find_word_backward, whose word_navigation.rs72-128 uses scalar indices; kill_word_forward at1071 and word movement1085-1095 likewise treat scalar results as bytes. With text '你' and byte cursor3, backward word lookup indexes beyond its one-character vector; from cursor0, forward word returns1 then drain(0..1) violates a UTF8 boundary. Movement can leave a cursor inside a codepoint. These are source-derived reachable failures from normal native shortcuts, not test executions. Native word tests1841-1873 are ASCII; multibyte tests2139-2168 cover character editing only.
entries.port: Use one explicit index representation throughout editing and convert at word-helper boundaries; preferably compute byte ranges from grapheme/word spans once. Repair these panic paths before expanding shortcuts. Preserve existing safe scalar-boundary setters while upgrading to grapheme boundaries, marker ownership and cross-line kill behavior.
entries.priority_reason: Current word shortcuts can panic or corrupt cursor position on normal non-ASCII text.

entries.title: Editor kill accumulation and multiline yank-pop replacement
entries.what: Accumulate only consecutive kills in direction order, then replace the prior yank when cycling the kill ring.
entries.mechanism: A kill captures an undo snapshot and prepends backward or appends forward deleted content to the current ring entry only when the prior action was kill; unrelated typing/navigation/replacement breaks accumulation. Newline boundary kills contribute LF. Yank captures once, inserts current ring value including multiple lines, sets lastAction='yank' and emits change. Yank-pop requires last action yank and ring length>1, captures once, deletes the exact previously yanked span ending at cursor, rotates persistent ring order, and inserts the replacement. The source deletion helper and insertion helper each emit onChange, so a successful yank-pop exposes an intermediate deletion callback. Undo restores editor/pastes, not kill-ring contents.
entries.interfaces: KillRing.peek/push/rotate; lastAction; multiline deleteYankedText; undo/onChange callbacks.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:592-673 has a ring and yank, but callers set last_action='kill' through push_undo before kill() checks it; later independent kills therefore accumulate into an existing ring regardless of intervening action. yank_pop only checks ring length, rotates and calls yank, with no prior-yank guard or removal of the earlier insertion, so it appends content and can run outside a yank chain. Native selection cut/copy/yank are additional capabilities to retain. The inline kill/yank test2071-2090 covers one entry and cannot establish cycling correctness.
entries.port: Capture previous action before transaction bookkeeping and store the actual inserted yank range or equivalent cursor/text identity. Replace that range atomically when cycling, reject stale chains after unrelated edits, and explicitly decide whether to preserve the source's two change callbacks or expose a strengthened atomic callback contract.
entries.priority_reason: Current native yank-pop changes prompt content by appending instead of replacing the previous yank.

entries.title: Editor marker-aware word wrapping and logical-to-visual ranges
entries.what: Wrap editor content at word/CJK opportunities while retaining source ranges needed for cursor movement, decoration and atomic paste markers.
entries.mechanism: wordWrapLine returns text plus UTF16 startIndex/endIndex for each chunk, preserving source whitespace and all original content. Prefer a break after whitespace before nonspace or around CJK; if backtracking still leaves the next wide segment over width, force-break before it. Split oversized registered marker segments recursively into ordinary graphemes for display while retaining logical atom identity. Empty input/nonpositive width yields an empty chunk. Layout maps hidden source positions to display positions, wraps each logical line, clips decoration spans to each chunk and assigns a boundary cursor to the next nonfinal chunk, with last chunk allowing end-of-line. Source defect: when a single real grapheme itself is wider than maxWidth, the oversized-segment recursive call receives the identical grapheme and width and has no progress guard. A width1 layout with a two-cell CJK character reaches this recursion; do not port it unchanged.
entries.interfaces: Exported wordWrapLine(line,maxWidth,segments?) -> WrappedLine[]; internal visual ranges and cursor flags; marker-aware grapheme segmentation.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:195-214 wraps Unicode scalars at hard cell width with no word/CJK opportunities or valid-marker atom metadata; it permits one overwide glyph rather than recursing. render at1390-1558 wraps the active logical line one column narrower than other logical lines, so moving cursor between rows changes wrapping. It does not supply a shared logical/visual map for movement or decoration. Preserve its bounded behavior for too-narrow terminals while implementing the source's intended content-preserving range model.
entries.port: Build one grapheme/atom layout map reused by render and navigation. Add safe progress for a grapheme wider than available width, explicitly choosing clipping/overflow/fallback policy and ensuring no lost content. Port source whitespace and backtrack cases rather than assuming generic wrap_ansi output carries editing offsets.
entries.priority_reason: The renderer and cursor must agree on wrapped positions, especially around wide glyphs and folded paste markers.

entries.title: Editor render-only decorations and concealed source prefixes
entries.what: Style or conceal input spans without inserting terminal codes into editor text or shifting the source cursor.
entries.mechanism: Decoration callback receives each logical line; exceptions become an empty list. Keep integer spans with0<=start<end<=line.length, sort by start and drop subsequent overlaps. concealPrefix is clamped to an integer0..span length; the protected first-line prompt prefix is also hidden. Build sourceToDisplay/displayToSource mappings per UTF16 code unit; concealed source positions map to a display boundary whose reverse map points after concealed text. Map accepted style prefix/suffix spans through concealment, clip them against wrapped chunk source ranges, and insert them around only the display substring. Cursor and edits remain in plain source coordinates. Validation is by code unit, not grapheme boundary, so the port must make any stronger boundary validation explicit.
entries.interfaces: EditorDecoration {start,end,prefix,suffix,concealPrefix?}; EditorDecorations callback; setDecorations; protected getPromptPrefixLength; source/display maps.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1390-1558 can reverse native selection and render a placeholder but has no decoration callback, concealed prefix contract or source/display maps. Native style.prompt at76-88 is stored but unused in render. Generic syntax/theme adapters belong TUI-005; the coding-agent literal highlighter and CustomEditor wrapper consume this primitive rather than replacing it.
entries.port: Add a render-only decoration API and explicit byte/source/display mapping. Retain native selection as a separate overlapping visual layer with defined ordering, isolate callback failures and never persist ANSI bytes into text. Wire coding-agent highlighters through the shared map so hidden mode prefixes and wrapped decorations preserve caret position.
entries.priority_reason: Input highlighting and mode-prefix concealment require a primitive contract that the native editor does not expose.

entries.title: Editor prompt gutter, borders, viewport and caret rendering
entries.what: Render a width-bounded editor with live appearance settings, visible caret, prompt gutter and a scrollable local viewport.
entries.mechanism: Normalize padding to finite floor>=0 and autocomplete visible rows to finite floor3..20(default5). Border style none/single/double/round/bold controls only horizontal top/bottom rows; round uses the horizontal single glyph. Appearance setters request render on changed values, decorations always request. Clamp padding to floor((width-1)/2); drop prompt if it would leave fewer than two text columns. Prompt uses borderColor and appears only on the first visual row, with equal-width spaces elsewhere. Content width subtracts both paddings and prompt; reserve one cursor cell only when padding is zero. Display at most max(5,floor(terminal.rows*.3)) body rows and adjust/clamp local scroll to keep caret visible. Scroll indicator borders use source hardcoded single glyph plus arrows/count and ANSI-aware truncation. Fake reverse cursor is always visible on a whole grapheme/atom or end space; hardware marker is additionally emitted when focused, including while completion is open. Pad every row to width; append completion below bottom border.
entries.interfaces: EditorOptions paddingX,prompt,borderStyle,autocompleteMaxVisible,decorations; live getters/setters; focused and CURSOR_MARKER; TUI terminal rows/requestRender.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1390-1591 renders all rows, never uses scroll_offset as a viewport, subtracts only left padding, has no prompt gutter/appearance setters and always emits single top/bottom borders. It has no source fake cursor; focused hardware marker may be emitted in both adjacent chunks because both include cursor==chunk end/start. insert_cursor_marker at218-246 stops an escape on the first final-range character, including '[' immediately after ESC, so later SGR digits can count as display characters when selection/placeholder styles precede the caret. Native working/elapsed display, placeholder and explicit border color are extra capabilities; tests1593-1769 intentionally advance working animation per render and should be preserved or explicitly integrated with timer ownership.
entries.port: Use the shared layout map for one caret location, correct ANSI-aware insertion, two-sided padding, live appearance and a bounded local viewport. Preserve native working/elapsed and placeholder features, but let the host own scheduling. Apply source-derived narrow prompt/scroll indicator/width tests without copying its overwide-grapheme recursion.
entries.priority_reason: Current native editor can consume the whole screen and places the caret inconsistently on styled or wrapped lines.

entries.title: Editor visual-row movement, sticky column and paste continuation traversal
entries.what: Move through wrapped visual rows, preserve a preferred column across short lines and resizing, and avoid getting trapped inside a folded paste marker.
entries.mechanism: Build visual rows from the same concealed/wrapped presentation used to render. Nonfinal wrap rows have maximum cursor offset length-1; final rows allow end. The source's 'visual column' is a display-string UTF16 offset, not a terminal cell count. When a shorter target clamps position, remember the desired column; restore it on a row that fits, but after rewrapping a now-interior source position the current visual offset takes precedence. setCursorCol clears preferred/snap state and clamps first-line lower bound to protected prompt prefix. Snap any multi-unit grapheme/marker interior to segment start and retain pre-snap logical position so the next move uses its original visual row. Moving down into a marker continuation whose desired position is still inside the marker skips continuation rows until after the atom; a desired position past the tail may land in following content. Pages move max(5,floor(rows*.3)) visual rows. Horizontal/word/edit actions reset sticky state; Right at final document end replaces preferred column with current position.
entries.interfaces: preferredVisualCol,snappedFrom; visual row map,source/display maps; moveCursor/pageUp/pageDown and setCursorCol.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:965-1042 moves Up/Down and pages by logical row with a clamped byte column; page_scroll is fixed10 logical rows. There is no preferred column, wrapped-row traversal, hidden-prefix map or marker continuation skipping, despite render producing multiple rows. set_cursor preserves valid byte boundaries, which is necessary but does not provide these visual semantics. Native editor inline tests for pages and movement use unwrapped ASCII and do not establish visual parity.
entries.port: Reuse the exact render layout for navigation, store preferred source/display position explicitly and keep byte/UTF16/cell units separate. Port the source transition table and marker continuation cases, while documenting any intentional improvement to cell-based navigation for wide glyphs instead of assuming the current source already uses cells.
entries.priority_reason: Cursor movement must traverse what the user sees and retain intent after narrowing the terminal or crossing short lines.

entries.title: Editor character-jump mode and UTF-8-safe search boundaries
entries.what: Enter a one-target jump mode, search forward/backward across logical lines, and cancel cleanly on another control action.
entries.mechanism: Either jump binding enters direction mode. While pending, either jump binding cancels; a printable decoded sequence or data with first codepoint>=32 is consumed as the target string, while nonprintable input cancels and then falls through to normal handling. Search is case-sensitive, forward from cursor+1 UTF16 unit and backward from cursor-1, then full subsequent/prior lines; no match leaves cursor unchanged. A match uses normal cursor setter and clears action grouping. Source backward lastIndexOf with negative position clamps to zero and can match the current position at index0 despite the skip-current comment; specify this as a source edge case, not a stronger exclusion guarantee.
entries.interfaces: jumpForward/jumpBackward key actions; jumpMode and jumpToChar(target,direction); multiline cursor state.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1098-1156 uses a char target but computes forward slice start as cursor byte offset+target.len_utf8 and backward as cursor-target.len_utf8 with an exclusive prefix. Target width is not the width of the character under/before the cursor. For '你x' at byte0 targeting ASCII x, line[1..] is an invalid UTF8 slice; ordinary jump can panic. Backward search also skips an immediately preceding target due to exclusive endpoint. Pending mode is consumed only by plain/Shift chars in hardcoded handle_key at1200-1388; repeated jump resets direction rather than canceling and control actions can leave mode pending. Inline jump tests1769-1840 are ASCII only.
entries.port: Compute search starts from actual next/previous grapheme or codepoint boundaries, keep ranges valid and define current-position exclusion explicitly. Implement pending-mode cancellation before normal action dispatch and retain multiline/case-sensitive matching. Include multibyte current character with ASCII target and immediate-backward-target cases in future regression validation.
entries.priority_reason: The current native jump path can panic on ordinary multibyte text; mode cancellation also differs visibly.

entries.title: Editor asynchronous completion scheduling, stale-result checks and menu acceptance
entries.what: Coordinate cancellable asynchronous suggestions with the current text/caret, explicit Tab force mode, menu navigation and atomic completion acceptance.
entries.mechanism: Provider replacement cancels prior work; default triggers @/# combine with unique provider single-code-unit nonwhitespace triggers except slash. Natural attachment-trigger requests debounce20ms; explicit or forced requests start immediately. Cancellation increments a start token, clears debounce timer and aborts active controller. Requests serialize by awaiting the previous task, then check current provider/enabled/token before capturing text+line+column, creating controller and incrementing request ID. On result require not aborted, enabled, matching IDs and exact text/caret snapshot; invalid/empty results close menu and request render. Exact case-sensitive value match then first prefix match selects best item. Natural and force menus retain their mode across updates; active cursor moves requery. Explicit forced singleton applies directly with undo/change/render; otherwise create SelectList with configured row cap and a narrow12..32 slash prefix column versus32 default. Tab accepts selected item and closes; Enter applies a prefix-starting-slash command then continues to submit, but other completion contexts only apply/close. Source limitations: the assignment at line2405 was connector-redacted and its contents were not recovered; surrounding token guards were read. There is no catch around prior-task/provider await, so rejected provider promises can poison later serialized requests; an abort-ignoring unresolved provider blocks subsequent requests. Editor has no dispose cleanup for these timers/tasks. Forced singleton return does not explicitly clear an already-existing menu.
entries.interfaces: setAutocompleteProvider,isShowingAutocomplete,protected isAutocompleteEnabled; AbortController,request IDs/debounce token; SelectList; provider.applyCompletion; requestRender/onChange.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1-2420 has no completion provider/menu/request lifecycle. Actual native host counterpart is rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/autocomplete.rs:12-201: synchronous provider calls on refresh/navigation/acceptance, centered bounded menu rendered in a separate container above editor, selection retained/clamped, explicit / or @ contexts alone consume Up/Down with clamped nonwrapping movement. It has no async debounce/abort/stale snapshot/force singleton or provider application hook. Acceptance re-queries rather than accepting a stored result and calls set_text, which clears paste registry and lacks undo snapshot. Preserve this existing host integration and byte-offset adapters, not a claim that native completion is wholly missing.
entries.port: Move request ownership into a reusable editor/controller contract with owned provider handles, cancellation, text/caret generation checks and a disposal path. Preserve native menu placement if intentionally configured while matching source action precedence, best-match and atomic acceptance. Recover safely from rejection and ignored cancellation without serial queue poisoning; document these as strengthened error handling beyond the current TS source.
entries.priority_reason: Async custom completion must not apply stale text, discard folded pastes or hang all later requests after a provider failure.

entries.title: SelectList filtering, configured navigation and callback lifetime
entries.what: Filter stable selection values, navigate matching items with shared bindings and deliver selection/cancel callbacks safely.
entries.mechanism: Constructor retains item references and initial filtered list. setFilter uses case-insensitive startsWith on item.value, preserving source order and resetting index0; labels do not participate. setSelectedIndex clamps to0..last and does not notify. Up/Down wrap and notify only when an item exists; confirm invokes onSelect only with a selected item; configured cancel invokes onCancel. Empty-list Up may set-1 internally and Down may later change it, but getSelectedItem safely returns null. There is no built-in search input or page action despite those generic action IDs existing. selectedPrefix is part of the theme interface but is not called by render.
entries.interfaces: SelectItem {value,label,description?}; SelectList.setFilter/setSelectedIndex/getSelectedItem; onSelect/onCancel/onSelectionChange; tui.select up/down/confirm/cancel.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/select_list.rs:238-419 uses fuzzy_filter on optional search_text (or value), changing membership/order from source prefix matching. This search_text support, persistent value-keyed multi-select at118-236 and page/Ctrl-j/k/n/p shortcuts at289-335 are useful native extras. Native hardcoded key handling ignores shared user overrides and Ctrl-C cancel; modified Up/Down/Enter are accepted solely by KeyCode. move_up/down invokes callbacks while selected_index and filtered_items mutexes remain held, so a selection-change callback that queries/changes list selection can deadlock. Callback mutexes are also held during invocation. Empty navigation is safely ignored and should remain so.
entries.port: Expose a source-compatible prefix filter mode while retaining native fuzzy/search_text and multi-select options. Route through configured actions, clone selected item/callback handles and release all list locks before user callbacks. Keep extra native navigation only where it does not override caller policy.
entries.priority_reason: Generic selectors must respect user bindings and allow callbacks to inspect or update selection without hanging.

entries.title: SelectList adaptive columns, custom truncation and shared chrome
entries.what: Render selected values and descriptions in width-bounded columns, retaining borders for empty results and caller-controlled primary text formatting.
entries.mechanism: Display label when truthy else value. Primary width is widest filtered label+2, clamped to normalized min/max bounds; absent bounds both default32, one bound sets both. Center maxVisible window around selection, clamp to ends and append selected/total when clipped. Description collapses runs of CR/LF to one space and trims; show it only when width>40 and remaining description budget>10, reserving prefix2, column gap2 and safety2. Selected style wraps prefix/value/description together; unselected description style wraps its spacing+text. Custom truncatePrimary receives text,maxWidth,columnWidth,item,isSelected; its output is always truncated again to maxWidth. Optional side-bearing chrome reserves two columns before rendering and wraps both normal and no-match results. No-match text without chrome is emitted without local width truncation, a source limitation.
entries.interfaces: SelectListLayoutOptions and SelectListTruncatePrimaryContext; SelectListTheme borderStyle/borderColor; centered visible window and scrollInfo.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/select_list.rs:421-604 largely preserves adaptive32-column layout, centered window and description threshold. It lacks chrome fields/wrapper and uses 'No matching items'. normalize_single_line replaces each newline/CR separately instead of collapsing runs. Custom truncate callback at520-535 receives only text/width/column width, ignores selection and item context, and its returned string is not bounded again; an overlong callback can exceed render width. Multi-select adds checkbox prefix width correctly and should remain available. Existing inline tests606-679 are basic selection/multi-select tests rather than TS custom-truncation/chrome cases.
entries.port: Extend native layout callback context with item and selection, enforce final width after callback, add shared border strategy/inner-width accounting and exact description normalization. Preserve native multi-select prefix geometry and use the source tests for min/max alignment and empty-result borders.
entries.priority_reason: Autocomplete and session/model selectors rely on consistent descriptions, custom labels and narrow-terminal geometry.

entries.title: SettingsList search, live item patching, value cycling and submenu ownership
entries.what: Edit settings in place with optional search and nested components, preserving selected row and current value across changes.
entries.mechanism: Optional enableSearch(defaultfalse) creates Input. updateValue mutates the first matching item reference; updateItem patches only provided label/description/currentValue fields, re-filters by label when search enabled and clamps selection. setMaxVisible clamps>=1; getItemCount returns unfiltered size. Up/Down wrap visible rows. Left/Right cycles values only when search disabled or query empty, otherwise belongs to search cursor; Enter always activates, Space activates only without query. Missing current value chooses first on forward or last on backward; every successful cycle updates item then calls onChange. Submenu takes precedence on activation, receives currentValue and done callback and completely replaces render/input until completion. done(undefined) cancels; any provided value updates/calls change, closes submenu and restores opening index. invalidate forwards to active submenu. No submenu dispose or multiple-done guard is present in source.
entries.interfaces: SettingItem {id,label,description,currentValue,values?,submenu(currentValue,done)}; SettingsListOptions.enableSearch; updateValue/updateItem/setMaxVisible/getItemCount; onChange/onCancel.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/settings_list.rs:17-376 has in-place forward cycles, navigation, programmatic fuzzy search and submenu notification; retain value_of,set_items and Boolean toggle extras. Its filter matches key instead of label, there is no integrated Input/enableSearch, Left/Right/backward cycle or user binding dispatch. has_submenu merely calls on_select(item); there is no child component/current-value/done ownership or forwarded render/input/invalidate. max_visible is fixed10 with no setter and updateItem/count absent. on_change/on_select/on_cancel callbacks execute under their callback mutexes, restricting reentrant callback replacement. update_value re-filters cloned rows but preserves/clamps numeric selection, which is useful existing behavior.
entries.port: Add optional search Input and explicit submenu state with a completion handle, route actions through shared bindings and implement backward cycling/live patch APIs. Preserve native external submenu adapters and settings persistence ownership, but make component lifetime/cleanup explicit and release callback locks before invocation.
entries.priority_reason: Settings and appearance dialogs need searchable live rows, reversible submenu navigation and both-direction adjustment.

entries.title: SettingsList responsive layout, selected descriptions and hint chrome
entries.what: Render a responsive settings viewport with aligned values, selected-row help, search and consistent border/hint behavior.
entries.mechanism: Active submenu renders at full requested width with no parent chrome. Main list reserves two columns for side-bearing borders. Optional search Input plus blank line precedes rows. Empty unfiltered list says 'No settings available' and shows hint only when search enabled; no matching filtered rows says 'No matching settings' and always shows hint. Center visible window around selection. Align labels against min(30,widest unfiltered label width), but do not independently truncate long labels; compute value budget from cursor width+alignment+two-space separator+safety2, then finally truncate entire row. Only selected item's description appears below rows after a blank line, ANSI-wrapped at width-4 and prefixed two spaces. Scroll count and final blank+hint use theme callbacks; hint text distinguishes Type to search and explains arrows/Enter/Space/Escape.
entries.interfaces: SettingsListTheme label(text,selected),value(text,selected),description,cursor,hint,borderStyle/borderColor; renderMainList; maxVisible.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/settings_list.rs:378-468 uses fixed label20/value15 truncation and no alignment padding, prints inline description on every row when room, and does not finally bound full row to supplied width. It lacks search rendering, selected-only wrapped help, instructional hint, dynamic row cap and chrome. Its theme has key/value/selected/selected_prefix functions without source selected flags/cursor/hint fields. Empty text differs and scroll count is not truncated. The main application can wrap this primitive, but the generic source contract is missing here.
entries.port: Replace fixed columns with measured responsive geometry and final ANSI-aware width enforcement, add source-compatible theme callbacks/selected description/hints and reserve border inner width. Keep application-specific chrome choices supplied by the caller.
entries.priority_reason: Narrow settings dialogs currently lose useful values and can emit rows wider than their allocated region.

entries.title: Markdown transform, cache, padding and default-style lifecycle
entries.what: Render Markdown through a width-aware transform and theme with predictable caching, full-line padding/background and protected image escape rows.
entries.mechanism:
Constructor copies options and retains theme/default style. Cache keys original source text and outer render width, returning cached array directly; setText and invalidate clear text/width/lines cache, but the separately cached defaultStylePrefix is not cleared. Compute contentWidth=max(1,width-2*paddingX), call optional transform(source,contentWidth) only on cache miss, and treat empty/whitespace transformed text as[] without padding. Normalize all tabs to three spaces. Parser instance is Marked with custom strict strike tokenizer (dependency pinned18.0.5); the token-producing expression at source245 was connector-redacted and not recovered. Render each token with next-type context, wrap nonimage rows, then add both margins and either full-width bg via applyBackgroundToLine or plain right padding. Image rows bypass wrap/margins/background. Vertical padding is full-width with optional background. Default foreground/bold/italic/strike/underline styling applies to text runs; background is deferred to row stage. Transform/theme exceptions are not caught.

Native cache coverage at rust:crates/ice-tui/tests/render_cache.rs:65-125 reads content/width/theme invalidation assertions. The Text theme test only checks a later content update; it does not itself compare theme-specific Text output.
entries.interfaces: Markdown(text,paddingX,paddingY,theme,defaultTextStyle?,options?); setText/invalidate; MarkdownOptions.transform,preserveOrderedListMarkers,preserveBackslashEscapes,tableStyle; DefaultTextStyle.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:20-173,923-958 caches content,width and global theme revision and returns cloned output, a useful native improvement to retain. entries.title: Markdown inline syntax, inherited styles and capability-aware hyperlinks
entries.what: Render inline Markdown without losing enclosing heading/quote/default styles, and choose clickable links or readable URL fallback from terminal capability.
entries.mechanism: Strict strike accepts exactly paired double tildes with nonspace/non-tilde boundaries and escaped content; single tilde remains literal. Escape tokens choose raw or decoded text via preserveBackslashEscapes. Text may recurse nested tokens and styles each newline-separated segment. Strong/em/code/link/del append enclosing stylePrefix after their own style reset, then strip repeated trailing enclosing prefixes so padding is unstyled. Prefixes are derived by styling a NUL sentinel. Links style+underline nested text and emit OSC8 when hyperlinks capability true; otherwise append parenthesized URL only if raw label differs from href and href stripped of mailto:. HTML tokens render raw text. br emits LF; unknown inline token with text falls back to that text, so image token normally contributes alt text without image retrieval. Heading/quote callers supply their own style contexts.
entries.interfaces: MarkdownTheme inline callbacks; DefaultTextStyle; preserveBackslashEscapes; terminal capabilities.hyperlinks and hyperlink(text,url).
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:410-565 uses pulldown-cmark with strikethrough and a prefixed single-line document plus nested frames. It supports CommonMark nesting, images and literal HTML, but has no strict-double-tilde customization or escape-preservation option. Code is trim()ed and padded into a themed background chip. Links always print a parenthesized URL when stripped label differs exactly; no OSC8 capability branch or mailto normalization. Native image fallback prints alt (or 'image') plus URL, a useful richer fallback to preserve if intentionally selected. Heading/quote wrappers do not restore their own foreground/bold/italic after nested resets; global base_style reopens only the configured base and cannot represent per-context inheritance. Generic Color reset differences remain owned by TUI-001 rather than duplicated here.
entries.port: Implement explicit inherited inline style contexts and capability-aware link rendering, with source syntax/escape options and safe style termination. Keep native nested parser and image fallback capabilities, but adapt them to the source contract; preserve a user-visible choice if code chips differ from theme-provided code style.
entries.priority_reason: Nested formatting and clickable links are frequent transcript behavior; losing enclosing style or duplicating URLs is visible and affects width.

entries.title: Markdown nested blocks, list markers, quote continuation and spacing
entries.what: Render parsed nested lists/quotes/headings with consistent source-aware markers, continuation indentation and one intentional inter-block gap.
entries.mechanism: Token hierarchy drives lists, quotes and block spacing. Headings1/2 hide hashes; level1 adds underline, all are bold+heading color, level>=3 retains '#'*level plus space. Heading/code/quote/hr/table add a blank only when a following token exists and is not space; paragraph also suppresses extra gap before list; space token emits one blank. HR width=min(contentWidth,80). Lists indent four spaces per parsed depth; ordered defaults number from token.start+i, unordered '- ', with optional preserveOrderedListMarkers retaining original1..9-digit . or ) and unordered -/+/* markers. Task adds '[x] ' or '[ ] ' after bullet. Continuations align after actual marker width; every child block is rendered recursively at reduced item width, nested lists recurse depth+1 and loose lists separate items. Quotes recursively render block tokens at width-2 with an identity inline default context, strip trailing empty quote rows, reapply quote+italic after embedded SGR0 and prepend '│ ' to every wrapped row, including lazy continuations.
entries.interfaces: MarkdownOptions.preserveOrderedListMarkers; parsed Token/ Tokens.List hierarchy; renderToken(nextTokenType,styleContext),renderList depth; MarkdownTheme heading(level),quote/quoteBorder/listBullet/hr.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:175-408,579-645 manually classifies each physical line before using inline parsing. Heading markers are hidden at every level and both h1/h2 underlined. Lists preserve ordered source numbers by default, use bullet'•'/task'☒' or'☐', indent two spaces at root and two per inferred leading-space depth, and only remember one continuation indent until a blank/nonindented row. There is no recursive block nesting or loose-list state; quote children/lazy continuation are ordinary lines and wrapped quote continuation uses spaces instead of repeating the border. HR uses startsWith('---' or'***'), so non-rule text can become a rule. Physical blank lines are preserved rather than normalized according to next token, and setext/reference/nested block semantics are not established by a full-document parser. Existing native prefix-aligned wrapping is useful but only partial.
entries.port: Use a real block tree/event parser for the whole document and preserve source markers needed by options. Build prefix-aware recursive rendering and spacing rules, retain native readable marker styles as configurable alternatives and port the nested quote/list/code/loose-list source cases. Do not infer parity from the presence of pulldown-cmark in the inline helper alone.
entries.priority_reason: LLM output routinely nests lists, quotes and code; the current line scanner changes structure and omits quote semantics.

entries.title: Markdown fenced code streaming, highlighting and native Mermaid preservation
entries.what: Keep streamed code block height stable without discarding real code, while retaining native optional diagram rendering behind an explicit policy.
entries.mechanism: Only inspect the final token, recursively following the final list item or blockquote; if it is code, extract an opening backtick/tilde run of length>=3 from raw token start. Trim a final line only when it consists solely of the same fence character and is shorter than the opener, removing its preceding newline from token.text. Interior short runs remain code. Render normalized visible opening '```'+lang, body lines from optional highlightCode(code,lang) or codeBlock styling, each with string codeBlockIndent(defaulttwo spaces), and closing '```'; preserve next-token spacing. Entire body is later ANSI-wrapped. TS primitive has no built-in Mermaid/LaTeX interpreter; caller transform/highlighter may provide richer output. Syntax theme adapter details remain in TUI-005.
entries.interfaces: MarkdownTheme.highlightCode/codeBlock/codeBlockBorder/codeBlockIndent; final-token streaming fence normalization; MarkdownOptions.transform.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:197-284,647-707 strips every1–2-character line composed of backticks and/or tildes before checking code state, including ordinary text and interior code. It records only fence character, not opening length, accepts any same-character >=3 prefix as closing even with trailing text, and normalizes tabs to4 only in code. Ordinary code hides fences/language and renders a padded themed surface using stateful native Highlighter; these are deliberate native presentation capabilities to retain as an option. Mermaid blocks buffer until a matching close and render Mermaid at239-243; an unclosed/streaming Mermaid buffer is never flushed. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/mermaid.rs:28-247 renders common flow edges and ->> sequence messages as text, preserving labels across edges, and falls back to source only if no recognized rows exist; mixed unsupported rows are dropped once any row is recognized. This is a native extra, not complete Mermaid language support.
entries.port: Replace global partial-fence suppression with parser-aware final-fence logic and track opener length/indent. Expose source-compatible code border/highlighter contract while retaining native code surfaces and optional Mermaid renderer. Preserve unclosed diagram content through a streaming fallback and do not silently lose unsupported constructs in a mixed diagram. No external diagram tool or network execution is required by this audit.
entries.priority_reason: Current native fence handling can erase legitimate text/code and hide an unfinished Mermaid response entirely.

entries.title: Markdown table column budgets and lossless multiline cells
entries.what: Fit tables into the content width while preserving complete cell content, styled long tokens and stable borders.
entries.mechanism: For N header columns reserve3N+1 border/padding cells. If remaining budget<N, fall back to wrapped token.raw. Measure styled natural width and longest whitespace-delimited word per column capped30, with minimum1. If word minima exceed budget, allocate1each then proportional floor growth weighted by max(wordMin-1,0), distributing remainder left-to-right. If natural table fits, use max(natural,min); otherwise distribute extra budget proportionally to natural-minus-min growth, then round-robin leftover without exceeding natural widths. Wrap every header/body cell at its allocated width using ANSI wrapper, render each logical row as max(cell heights) physical rows and pad shorter cells. Bold all header cell padding/text; body rows retain inline styling. Source ignores parsed alignment metadata—its alignment test checks presence only, not right/center placement.
entries.interfaces: renderTable(token,availableWidth,nextTokenType,styleContext); getLongestWordWidth cap30; wrapCellText; inline width and ANSI wrap contracts.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:720-868 detects only rows starting/ending pipe, manually splits escaped/code pipes with a one-bit backtick toggle, and uses proportional rounded natural widths with minimum1. It budgets3N+1 but emits compact borders without source cell padding, has no word minima/remainder reconciliation/narrow raw fallback, and truncates each cell to one line with ellipsis. Thus table text is lost instead of wrapped. Header is not bold. The splitter handles simple one-backtick spans but toggling each backtick does not model multi-backtick code delimiters. Existing native row dividers and Unicode grid should be preserved while repairing layout.
entries.port: Feed table nodes from the block parser into deterministic width allocation and lossless cell wrapping. Preserve escaped and multi-backtick pipe syntax using parser tokens, restore header emphasis/cell padding and explicitly document alignment as unsupported unless intentionally added. Cover narrow budgets, long URLs/inline code and multirow cells from the fully read TS tests.
entries.priority_reason: Truncated table cells can hide material answer content and commands; source behavior preserves them through wrapping.

entries.title: Markdown table style policy and default invalidation
entries.what: Expose the source table styles and per-instance/process-default precedence while preserving a consistent shared column layout.
entries.mechanism: Per-instance tableStyle wins over process default(initial'unicode'). Unicode and ASCII emit top/header/body separators/bottom; clean retains vertical cell separators/padding but no horizontal borders; clean-top-bottom adds continuous horizontal top/bottom only; raw wraps original Markdown. All styles use the same3N+1 column geometry and multiline cell pass. setDefaultTableStyle changes a module variable and getDefaultTableStyle returns it; cached existing Markdown output is not invalidated automatically, so caller must invalidate to apply a changed default. Source accepts typed style values with no runtime validation; invalid foreign JS values can fail when glyphs are accessed.
entries.interfaces: MarkdownTableStyle union; setDefaultTableStyle/getDefaultTableStyle; per-instance options.tableStyle.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:746-831 has only one compact Unicode table strategy and no default/instance style control. Native global theme revision participates in Markdown caching at923-948, so it provides a useful invalidation mechanism to retain when table policy changes. The main application's appearance setting alone does not implement these glyph/layout choices in this primitive.
entries.port: Add explicit table style policy using the shared layout and wire appearance-triggered cache invalidation through the caller. Preserve native theme-revision cache invalidation and keep storage/UI ownership in the main TUI area. Use one layout pass so switching border glyphs does not accidentally alter wrapping.
entries.priority_reason: Appearance table preferences currently have no primitive implementation and existing cached messages need an intentional update path.

entries.title: Bounded Kitty upload reuse and placement redraw transactions
entries.what: Reuse already uploaded image data across moves and short offscreen intervals while bounding retained offscreen image count and estimated memory.
entries.mechanism:
Each image redraw parses placement metadata for every screen line. Visible IDs are recorded, and their cache entry is deleted/reinserted in Map order with current transmissionGeneration, transmissionBytes and estimatedDecodedBytes. Same-generation cached IDs use the lossless placement-only replacement line; changed generations retain the full transmission. Repeated visibility therefore refreshes retention order. Only offscreen entries count toward limits: at most16 images,32MiB transmission bytes and64MiB estimated decoded raster bytes. Evict oldest offscreen entries until all three limits hold, concatenate per-ID deleteKittyImage commands, and never evict an on-screen ID merely to meet these offscreen limits. This is not a total process/terminal-memory cap.

Cache preparation runs only for a full frame redraw or a changed row involving an old/new image, and only for captured Kitty protocol. Full redraw with an existing cache deletes all placements but preserves data; without cached uploads it deletes all Kitty image data. Image-only changes delete placements, then evicted data IDs are deleted before repaint. Every viewport row is repainted in image transactions so surrounding HStack text survives. previousScreen retains original transmission lines, not placement substitutions. Start clears cache; stop deletes Kitty data and clears it. Cropping/generation and encoded parsing are separate prerequisites. Source tests read image movement preserving siblings, reentry reuse,17th-offscreen count eviction and decoded quota; they were not executed.
entries.interfaces: Internal CachedKittyImage,prepareKittyScreen and terminal-owned upload map; getKittyImagePlacement generation and byte estimates; deleteAllKittyPlacements vs deleteAllKittyImages/deleteKittyImage; visible/offscreen frame identity.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tui_alt_screen.rs:908-1054 tracks prior rows and emits removed-image cleanup but has no generation-indexed upload map, offscreen LRU quotas, placement-only reuse or all-rows image transaction. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal_image.rs:249-281 deletes changed old placements by scanning image IDs; that row cleanup is useful existing behavior and does not provide retained data ownership. The full native renderer and its inline tests were read, not run.
entries.port: Add a terminal-owned upload cache over the metadata/parser service from TUI-227, keeping data versus placement deletion explicit. Count only offscreen data for the source retention policy, invalidate on protocol/terminal lifecycle changes and preserve unchanged surrounding line fragments when replacing transmission spans.
entries.priority_reason: Without bounded reuse, image scrolling repeatedly uploads large payloads or accumulates terminal state; lossless row substitution must preserve neighboring text.

entries.title: Shared chrome border families and narrow-width gate
entries.what: Apply one shared border-family contract to selectors and compatible chrome while leaving theme selection to the application adapter.
entries.mechanism:
chromeBorderGlyphs returns one of11 families or null for none/unrecognized input. Exact corners/horizontal/vertical are: single(┌┐└┘,─,│),double(╔╗╚╝,═,║),round(╭╮╰╯,─,│),bold(┏┓┗┛,━,┃),single-double(┌┐╚╝,─,║),double-single(╔╗└┘,═,│),classic(++++,-,|),plus top-bottom-single/double/bold using only─/═/━ and no corners/sides. The mixed families deliberately use their listed top/bottom corners with one shared horizontal character; do not substitute a convention inferred from names.

applyChromeBorder returns the original lines unchanged for null glyphs or width<3, including top-bottom-only families; this means the comment's universal width guarantee does not hold on that bypass. Otherwise side families use inner=width-2 and top-bottom families inner=width. It always emits a colored top and bottom row, even for empty content, truncates each content row with ellipsis to inner width, pads by visible cell width and separately colors only side glyphs. The caller supplies lines already laid out at desired content width; the wrapper does not rerender a component. Color functions are assumed width-preserving.
entries.interfaces: ChromeBorderStyle union; chromeBorderGlyphs(style) -> {tl,tr,bl,br,h,v,sides}|null; applyChromeBorder(lines,width,style,color) -> string[]. Theme-to-family adapter remains main TUI-005.

entries.port: Implement the shared glyph map and width-gated wrapper in crates/ice-tui and use it from compatible selectors. Keep style resolution/theme updates in the main adapter, and preserve the exact bypass and empty-content rules; combine with corrected ANSI/grapheme truncation.
entries.priority_reason: A shared implementation keeps appearance border selections consistent across primitive selectors without duplicating family-specific layout.
